docs.title: Machine learning
docs.text:
General patterns

  • Name an experiment for the question it answers, and a run for one try: experiment, run
  • Name a model for what it predicts, and a model version for one trained copy: churn_classifier, churn_classifier version 7
  • Keep the data, the code and the result of a run apart: dataset_version, git_commit, metric
  • Name a metric with its split: val_accuracy, test_auc
  • Name a feature for the thing and the window: customer_orders_count_30d

Useful tips

  • Use snake_case for parameters and metrics. MLflow accepts many characters, but a plain name is easy to query
  • Use X_train, y_train only inside a short function. Use full names for fields that you store
  • Use dataset_version and a hash, not data_v2_final
  • Use an alias such as champion for the version that serves traffic. MLflow aliases replace the older stages

General anti-patterns

  • model for the code, the weights and the service at once
  • data2, data_new, final_final
  • acc and accuracy for different things in two runs
  • A metric with no split: loss
  • prod as a model name

The words follow MLflow Tracking and the MLflow Model Registry: Experiment, Run, Param, Metric, Artifact, Registered Model, Model Version. MLflow run statuses are RUNNING, SCHEDULED, FINISHED, FAILED and KILLED. The model version stages None, Staging, Production and Archived are deprecated in favor of aliases and tags.

docs.title: Entities
docs.text:
Entity Meaning Table Notes Experiment A group of runs for one question. experiments MLflow Experiment. Run One execution of training or evaluation. runs MLflow Run. Parameter An input value of a run. run_params A key and a value. Metric A number that a run measures. run_metrics A key, a value, a step, a time. Tag A label on a run or a model. run_tags Artifact A file that a run makes. artifacts A plot, a model file. Dataset A named source of data. datasets Dataset version A fixed snapshot of a dataset. dataset_versions Has a hash. Feature A column that a model reads. features Feature view A group of features with one source. feature_views Label The true answer for an example. labels Training job A job that runs training. training_jobs Pipeline A list of steps that make a model. pipelines Model A named model in the registry. models MLflow: registered model. Model version One trained copy of a model. model_versions A number, 1, 2, 3. Model alias A name that points to a version. model_aliases champion, challenger. Evaluation A test of a model version on a dataset. evaluations Deployment A model version that runs in an environment. deployments Endpoint The address that serves predictions. endpoints Prediction One answer of a model. predictions Often not stored in a database. Drift report A report on the change of data. drift_reports Prompt A text template for a language model. prompts

MLflow keeps experiments, runs, parameters, metrics and tags in its own store. The tables above matter only if you mirror them. The worked example keeps only the registry link.

docs.title: States
docs.text:
Entity States Run (MLflow) RUNNING, SCHEDULED, FINISHED, FAILED, KILLED Model version (MLflow) PENDING_REGISTRATION, FAILED_REGISTRATION, READY Model version stage (deprecated in MLflow) None, Staging, Production, Archived Training job queued, running, succeeded, failed, canceled Deployment creating, ready, degraded, failed, retiring, retired Dataset version draft, validated, deprecated

MLflow writes these states in upper case. If you mirror MLflow exactly, keep its values. Otherwise store lower case (ready) and map at the boundary. The worked example below keeps the MLflow values. The deployment states are the choice of this guide and are lower case. A training job maps to a run: running to RUNNING, succeeded to FINISHED, failed to FAILED, canceled to KILLED.

docs.title: Actions
docs.text:
Action Function name Meaning Trap Start a run mlflow.start_run Opens a run. Use it as a context manager. Log a parameter mlflow.log_param Stores an input value. A param is a string. Log a metric mlflow.log_metric Stores a number. Add a step for a curve. Log an artifact mlflow.log_artifact Stores a file. Log a model mlflow.<flavor>.log_model Stores a model in a run. For example mlflow.sklearn.log_model. It is registered only if you pass registered_model_name. Register a model mlflow.register_model Adds a version to the registry. Fit fit Trains on data. Not train_model in a class that has fit. Predict predict Gives an answer. predict_proba gives a probability. Evaluate evaluate_model Measures on a test set. Do not use the training set. Split split_dataset Makes train, validation and test sets. Fix the random seed. Promote MlflowClient.set_registered_model_alias Points an alias to a version. The old term is a stage transition. Deploy deploy_model_version Starts serving. Roll back rollback_deployment Returns to the last good version. Detect drift detect_drift Compares live data to training data.

Names with the mlflow. prefix or MlflowClient are MLflow APIs. The other names are wrappers in your own application.

docs.title: Traps
docs.text: Trap Why it is a problem Better model Code, weights and service are different. model for the registry name, model_version for the weights, endpoint for the service. experiment and run A run is one try. An experiment is the group. experiment_id, run_id. loss Training or validation? train_loss, val_loss. acc and accuracy Two names in two runs. accuracy with a split: val_accuracy. data_v2_final The name tells nothing and the file can change. dataset_version with a hash. train, test, val, eval, dev Names for splits vary. train, validation, test in stored fields. val_ only as a metric prefix. X and y Fine in a formula, vague in a field. features and labels in stored fields. feature A column, a feature view or a flag? feature for the model input. A feature flag is a different thing. prod An environment or a version? production environment, and an alias champion. stage Pipeline stage or model stage? pipeline_step and model_alias. target, label, y Three words for the answer. label for a stored true answer, target for the column name in a training table. score A probability, a metric or a ranking? predicted_probability, metric_value, ranking_score. seed Which one? split_seed for a split, training_seed for the model.

import mlflow


def train_churn_classifier(dataset_version: str, learning_rate: float) -> str:
    mlflow.set_experiment("churn_prediction")
    with mlflow.start_run(run_name="churn_classifier") as run:
        mlflow.log_param("dataset_version", dataset_version)
        mlflow.log_param("git_commit", current_git_commit())
        mlflow.log_param("learning_rate", learning_rate)
        model = fit_classifier(dataset_version, learning_rate)
        mlflow.log_metric("val_accuracy", evaluate_accuracy(model, split="validation"))
        mlflow.log_metric("val_auc", evaluate_auc(model, split="validation"))
        mlflow.sklearn.log_model(model, name="model", registered_model_name="churn_classifier")
        return run.info.run_id

docs.title: Payments
docs.text:
General patterns

  • Name the intent to pay, the attempt to pay and the movement of money as three separate entities: payment_intent, payment_attempt, charge
  • Name the actor with the word that the payment network uses: customer, merchant, acquirer, issuer
  • Keep the amount in minor units with a currency code: amount_cents, currency_code. Never use a float
  • Use a past participle for a state (captured) and a verb for an action (capture)
  • Give each money movement its own entity with its own states: refund, dispute, payout

Useful tips

  • Use authorized_amount_cents, captured_amount_cents and refunded_amount_cents when the amounts differ. A single amount hides the difference
  • Use an idempotency key on each create call: idempotency_key
  • Use the id of the provider as provider_payment_intent_id, and keep your own id
  • Store the reason of a failure as a code and a message: failure_code, failure_message

General anti-patterns

  • payment for the intent, the attempt and the money movement at once
  • status for the status of the payment and of the refund in the same field
  • amount with no unit and no currency
  • paid as the state of a payment or an intent. It does not say authorized or captured. paid is fine for a payout, as in Stripe
  • card_number in a database column. Store a token and the last four digits

The page uses Stripe words for the examples. Stripe is a de facto reference. The message names of bank-to-bank payments come from ISO 20022 and are in the table below.

docs.title: Entities
docs.text: Entity Meaning Table Notes Customer The payer, as the payment system knows them. customers Merchant The business that receives the money. merchants In a platform: a connected account. Payment method A way to pay that a customer saved. payment_methods A card, a bank account, a wallet. Card A card as a payment method. cards Keep a token, last4, brand, expiry_month, expiry_year. Payment intent The plan to collect one amount from one customer. payment_intents Has the whole lifecycle. Payment attempt One try to pay for an intent. payment_attempts An intent can have many. Charge The result of an attempt on a card or a method. charges Stripe: Charge. Authorization A hold of funds on a card. authorizations Expires in days. Capture The taking of held funds. captures Can be partial. Refund Money returned to the payer. refunds Linked to a payment intent. Dispute A payer asks the bank to reverse a charge. disputes Often called a chargeback. Strictly, the chargeback is the reversal. Payout Money sent from the provider to the merchant bank account. payouts Settlement batch A group of charges that the acquirer settles together. settlement_batches Balance transaction A line that changes the merchant balance. balance_transactions Charges, fees, refunds, payouts. Fee A cost of the provider for a charge. fees Transfer A move of money between two accounts of the provider. transfers Not a payout. Mandate The permission to debit a bank account again. mandates SEPA, ACH. Invoice payment A payment for an invoice. invoice_payments See SaaS. Webhook event A message from the provider about a change. webhook_events Store the id to remove duplicates. Idempotency key A unique key for a create call. column idempotency_key Not a table in most designs.

docs.title: Payment intent
docs.text: State Meaning Next states requires_payment_method The intent has no method yet, or the last try failed. requires_confirmation, processing, succeeded, canceled requires_confirmation The intent waits for the confirm call. requires_action, processing, requires_capture, succeeded, canceled requires_action The payer must do a step (3-D Secure). processing, requires_capture, succeeded, requires_payment_method, canceled processing The provider processes the payment. requires_capture, succeeded, requires_payment_method requires_capture The funds are held and wait for capture. succeeded, canceled succeeded The funds are taken. none canceled The intent is stopped. none

docs.title: Other entities
docs.text:
Entity States Charge pending, succeeded, failed Refund pending, requires_action, succeeded, failed, canceled Dispute warning_needs_response, warning_under_review, warning_closed, needs_response, under_review, won, lost Payout pending, in_transit, paid, failed, canceled Settlement batch open, closed, settled

The first table follows Stripe PaymentIntent. The other lists follow Stripe where Stripe has the object. Stripe adds states in new API versions, so check the version you use. The settlement batch states are community practice.

docs.title: Actions
docs.text: Action Function name Meaning Trap Create an intent create_payment_intent Records the plan to collect money. No money moves yet. Attach a method attach_payment_method Links a method to a customer. Confirm an intent confirm_payment_intent Starts the attempt. Authorize authorize_payment_intent Holds funds. A hold is not a payment. Capture capture_payment_intent Takes held funds. Partial capture is allowed. Void void_authorization Releases a hold. Not a refund. In the Stripe model, a void is cancel_payment_intent from requires_capture. Use void_authorization for your own authorization entity. Refund refund_payment_intent Returns money after capture. Full or partial. Cancel an intent cancel_payment_intent Stops an intent before success. Respond to a dispute submit_dispute_evidence Sends proof to the bank. Create a payout create_payout Sends the balance to the bank. Reconcile reconcile_settlement Matches the bank file to your records. Handle a webhook handle_webhook_event Applies a provider event once. Use the event id. Retry retry_payment_attempt Tries again with the same intent. New attempt, same intent.

docs.title: Message names (ISO 20022)
docs.text:
Bank-to-bank messages use a fixed family of names. The short form is a message identifier. Use the full name in code and the short form in comments.

Message Short form Meaning Customer credit transfer initiation pain.001 The customer asks the bank to send money. Customer payment status report pain.002 The bank reports the status of a request. Customer direct debit initiation pain.008 The creditor asks to debit an account. Financial institution credit transfer pacs.008 One bank asks another bank to send money. Payment return pacs.004 One bank returns a payment. Bank to customer statement camt.053 The statement of an account. Bank to customer debit credit notification camt.054 A notice of one or more entries.

docs.title: Traps
docs.text: Trap Why it is a problem Better payment for everything The intent, the try and the money are different things. payment_intent, payment_attempt, charge. authorize and capture as one word A hold and a capture have different states and amounts. authorized_at and captured_at. cancel, void, refund, reverse Four words for stopping a payment. cancel the intent (in Stripe this also releases a hold), void for your own authorization entity, refund a capture, reverse in the ledger. refund and chargeback The merchant starts a refund. The payer starts a dispute. refund and dispute. chargeback and dispute A chargeback is the reversal. A dispute is the case. dispute for the case and chargeback only for the reversal. transfer and payout A transfer moves money between accounts of the provider. A payout leaves to a bank. transfer and payout. settlement and payout The acquirer settles. The provider pays out. Keep both words with their own entity. fee and commission and markup Three words for the cost. fee for the provider cost, application_fee for a platform cut. amount Authorized, captured or refunded? authorized_amount_cents, captured_amount_cents, refunded_amount_cents. status = paid It hides authorized and captured. succeeded for a Stripe intent. captured as a flag or a state of your own charge. paid stays correct for a payout. card for a token A card number must never be in your data. card_token, last4, brand. reference Whose reference? merchant_reference, provider_payment_intent_id, bank_reference. currency A code or a symbol? currency_code with ISO 4217 (USD).

docs.text:
Inside a table, the status column is just status. Code and DTOs keep the full name, for example payment_intent_status. The column requested_amount_cents is the amount that the merchant asked for. The key idempotency_key is unique in the whole table here. Stripe scopes keys per account, so a system with many merchants adds merchant_id to the constraint. The table customers is not shown.

CREATE TABLE payment_intents (
    id                      bigint GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY,
    customer_id             bigint NOT NULL,
    requested_amount_cents  bigint NOT NULL,
    captured_amount_cents   bigint NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    refunded_amount_cents   bigint NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    currency_code           char(3) NOT NULL,
    status                  text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'requires_payment_method',
    idempotency_key         text NOT NULL,
    provider_payment_intent_id text,
    created_at              timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
    CONSTRAINT pk_payment_intents PRIMARY KEY (id),
    CONSTRAINT fk_payment_intents_customers FOREIGN KEY (customer_id) REFERENCES customers (id),
    CONSTRAINT uq_payment_intents_idempotency_key UNIQUE (idempotency_key),
    CONSTRAINT chk_payment_intents_status_allowed CHECK (status IN (
        'requires_payment_method', 'requires_confirmation', 'requires_action',
        'processing', 'requires_capture', 'succeeded', 'canceled'
    )),
    CONSTRAINT chk_payment_intents_currency_code_format CHECK (currency_code ~ '^[A-Z]{3}$'),
    CONSTRAINT chk_payment_intents_requested_amount_cents_positive CHECK (requested_amount_cents > 0),
    CONSTRAINT chk_payment_intents_captured_within_requested CHECK (captured_amount_cents <= requested_amount_cents),
    CONSTRAINT chk_payment_intents_refunded_within_captured CHECK (refunded_amount_cents <= captured_amount_cents)
);

CREATE INDEX idx_payment_intents_customer_id ON payment_intents (customer_id);

CREATE TABLE refunds (
    id                  bigint GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY,
    payment_intent_id   bigint NOT NULL,
    amount_cents        bigint NOT NULL,

def capture_payment_intent(intent: PaymentIntent, capture_amount_cents: int | None = None) -> PaymentIntent:
    if intent.payment_intent_status != "requires_capture":
        raise PaymentIntentStateError(intent.id, intent.payment_intent_status)
    captured_amount_cents = intent.requested_amount_cents if capture_amount_cents is None else capture_amount_cents
    if captured_amount_cents > intent.requested_amount_cents:
        raise AmountTooLargeError(intent.id, captured_amount_cents)
    return intent.with_capture(captured_amount_cents)

docs.title: SaaS
docs.text:
General patterns

  • Name the customer of the product account, and the person who signs in user. Keep the two apart
  • Name what the customer buys (plan), what they have now (subscription) and what they may use (entitlement) as three entities
  • Name the bill invoice and each line of it invoice_item
  • Name the use of the product with a meter: meter, usage_record
  • Give each tenant-owned table an account_id so that data stays apart

Useful tips

  • Use workspace or project for a group inside an account, and pick one word for the whole product
  • Use seat for a paid place for a user. A seat is not a user
  • Use trial_ends_at, current_period_start and current_period_end for time limits. current_period_start and current_period_end follow Stripe and are a deliberate exception to the _at rule. In newer Stripe API versions they live on the subscription item. trial_ends_at is the name of this guide for the Stripe field trial_end
  • Use feature_key for the code name of a feature, and plan_code for the code name of a plan

General anti-patterns

  • user for the customer who pays and the person who signs in
  • plan for the product plan, the price and the subscription at once
  • status that mixes billing state and access state
  • premium or is_pro as a boolean on the user. Use an entitlement
  • A plan name in code: if plan == "Gold". Check an entitlement

The billing words follow Stripe Billing (Customer, Product, Price, Subscription, Invoice). Payment words are in Payments.

On this page account is the paying customer. It maps to the Stripe Customer, not to the Stripe Account (the seller). In Payments the same party is customer_id.

docs.text: Trap Why it is a problem Better user A person who signs in and a customer who pays are different. user signs in. account pays. customer Stripe calls the payer a customer. Your product may call it an account. account, with provider_customer_id for the Stripe id. plan A plan, a price and a subscription differ. plan for the package, price for the cost, subscription for the account link. organization, account, tenant, workspace Four words for a group. account for the payer, workspace for a sub-group. tenant_id only for the isolation technique in shared tables. member and user A member is a user in one account. membership for the link. seat and license Two words for a paid place. seat. limit and quota Two words for a cap. limit is also a reserved SQL word. limit_value for the cap on the plan, usage for the count. docs.title: Worked example
docs.text:
The tables plans, prices and subscription_items are not shown. A subscription item holds the price. The value NULL in entitlements.limit_value means no limit, 0 means off, and a positive number is the cap.

CREATE TABLE accounts (
    id          bigint GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY,
    name        text NOT NULL,
    status      text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'active',
    created_at  timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
    CONSTRAINT pk_accounts PRIMARY KEY (id),
    CONSTRAINT chk_accounts_status_allowed CHECK (status IN ('active', 'suspended', 'closed'))
);

CREATE TABLE subscriptions (
    id                      bigint GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY,
    account_id              bigint NOT NULL,
    plan_id                 bigint NOT NULL,
    status                  text NOT NULL,
    trial_ends_at           timestamptz,
    current_period_start    timestamptz NOT NULL,
    current_period_end      timestamptz NOT NULL,
    cancel_at_period_end    boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT false,
    canceled_at             timestamptz,
    CONSTRAINT pk_subscriptions PRIMARY KEY (id),
    CONSTRAINT fk_subscriptions_accounts FOREIGN KEY (account_id) REFERENCES accounts (id),
    CONSTRAINT fk_subscriptions_plans FOREIGN KEY (plan_id) REFERENCES plans (id),
    CONSTRAINT chk_subscriptions_current_period_end_after_start CHECK (current_period_end > current_period_start),
    CONSTRAINT chk_subscriptions_status_allowed CHECK (status IN (
        'incomplete', 'incomplete_expired', 'trialing', 'active',
        'past_due', 'canceled', 'unpaid', 'paused'
    ))
);

CREATE INDEX idx_subscriptions_account_id ON subscriptions (account_id);
CREATE INDEX idx_subscriptions_plan_id ON subscriptions (plan_id);

CREATE TABLE features (
    id              bigint GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY,
    feature_key     text NOT NULL,
    CONSTRAINT pk_features PRIMARY KEY (id),
    CONSTRAINT uq_features_feature_key UNIQUE (feature_key)
);

CREATE TABLE entitlements (
    account_id      bigint NOT NULL,
    feature_key     text NOT NULL,
    limit_value     bigint,
    CONSTRAINT pk_entitlements PRIMARY KEY (account_id, feature_key),
    CONSTRAINT fk_entitlements_accounts FOREIGN KEY (account_id) REFERENCES accounts (id),
    CONSTRAINT fk_entitlements_features FOREIGN KEY (feature_key) REFERENCES features (feature_key),
    CONSTRAINT chk_entitlements_limit_value_non_negative CHECK (limit_value >= 0)
);

CREATE INDEX idx_entitlements_feature_key ON entitlements (feature_key);

PATCH /v1/subscriptions/{subscription_id}                   set cancel_at_period_end
GET  /v1/accounts/{account_id}/entitlements                 list the entitlements

    entitlement = account.entitlements.get(feature_key)

docs.title: Languages
docs.text:
General patterns

  • Follow the style guide of the language. A reader of that language expects its case style
  • Keep the meaning of a name the same in every language. Only the case style changes: order_total in Python, orderTotal in Java, OrderTotal in C#
  • Use the formatter and the linter of the language to enforce case. A tool is more reliable than a review comment

Useful tips

  • Start with the matrix below. Open the page of the language for details and examples
  • When code crosses a language border (an API, a database, a message), the border format wins. See Naming patterns and Databases
  • A style guide that is not official is marked in the matrix. Pick the one that your team uses and write it down

General anti-patterns

  • Copying the case style of one language into another: get_user_name() in Java, UserName for a local variable in Go
  • Mixing two styles in one project, for example camelCase and snake_case JSON keys in one API

docs.title: C# and .NET
docs.text:
General patterns

  • Use PascalCase for types, methods, properties, events, constants and namespaces: OrderService, CalculateTotal, MaxRetryCount
  • Use camelCase for local variables and parameters: orderTotal, couponCode
  • Start an interface name with I: IOrderRepository
  • Use a verb first for methods and a noun for properties, as in the action and context pattern
  • Name a file after the main type in it: OrderService.cs. This is common practice, and StyleCop checks it (SA1649)

Useful tips

  • Use _camelCase for private fields if your team follows the C# coding conventions. The .NET naming guidelines target public API and do not use underscores
  • End an async method name with Async: GetOrderAsync. This is a strong convention of the .NET libraries
  • Use an analyzer to enforce the rules (.editorconfig naming rules with the IDE1006 diagnostic, or StyleCop)

General anti-patterns

  • SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE for constants. C# uses PascalCase: MaxRetryCount
  • Hungarian notation: strName, iCount
  • Underscores in type and method names: Order_Service. Test method names are a common exception
  • A boolean that is not a statement: Status, Flag, Check

docs.title: Names by kind
docs.text: Kind Rule Examples Why this name Namespace PascalCase, dotted: Company.Product.Feature Shop.Orders, Contoso.Billing.Invoices The guidelines use this form, so a type name is unique across libraries. Class PascalCase noun OrderService, PaymentGateway The guidelines ask for PascalCase for every public type. Static class PascalCase noun OrderIds, Guard A class without instances. Extension class (community practice) the extended type plus Extensions StringExtensions, EnumerableExtensions Common practice in the .NET libraries. Struct PascalCase noun Money, OrderId A struct is a type, so it follows the type rule. Record PascalCase noun OrderLine A record is a type, so it follows the type rule. Interface I plus PascalCase IOrderRepository, IDisposable The I is a firm .NET convention. Enum singular PascalCase noun OrderStatus One value is one status. Flags enum plural PascalCase noun FilePermissions Several values can combine. Enum member PascalCase OrderStatus.Pending Same style as a constant. Constant PascalCase MaxRetryCount, DefaultTimeout The .NET guidelines use PascalCase. Static readonly field, public or internal PascalCase DefaultOptions It acts like a constant. A private one is s_camelCase; see Private names. Method verb first, PascalCase CalculateTotal, FindOrders An action. Async method method name plus Async GetOrderAsync, SaveAsync Callers see that they must await. Property PascalCase noun Total, CustomerEmail The guidelines ask for PascalCase for public members. Boolean property Is, Has, Can plus a word IsActive, HasGiftWrap, CanRefund A boolean reads as a statement. Event verb phrase, past or present OrderPlaced, Closing Past tense for after, -ing for before. Event raiser On plus the event name OnOrderPlaced The protected virtual method that raises the event (guidelines). Event handler method source, _, event Button_Click The IDE designer form. It is not a guideline rule. Delegate for an event the event name plus EventHandler OrderPlacedEventHandler The guidelines use this suffix for event delegates. Delegate for a callback the purpose plus Callback RetryCallback The guidelines use this suffix for delegates passed to methods. Attribute PascalCase plus Attribute RequiredAttribute The suffix can be dropped at use: [Required]. Exception PascalCase plus Exception OrderNotFoundException The guidelines require the suffix. Generic parameter T when it is clear; otherwise T plus a descriptive name T, TKey, TValue The guidelines use a single T only when it is self-explanatory. Local variable camelCase noun orderTotal, customerEmail The guidelines ask for camelCase for parameters, and the coding conventions use it for locals. Parameter camelCase noun orderId, couponCode The guidelines ask for camelCase for parameters. Private field _camelCase _orderRepository, _cache The C# coding conventions page (identifier names). Private static field s_camelCase s_instanceCount The C# coding conventions and the .NET runtime style use this form. Collection (community practice) plural noun Orders, LineItems A plural shows a list. Test class (community practice) class under test plus Tests OrderServiceTests Readers and file search find the tests of a class. Test method Method_Condition_Result (community practice) CalculateTotal_WithCoupon_AppliesDiscount The underscores split three parts. Test names are the usual exception to the no-underscore rule.

docs.title: Go
docs.text:
General patterns

  • Use MixedCaps and no underscores in Go names: orderTotal, OrderTotal, not order_total. The exceptions are test names (TestX_WithCoupon), example names (Example_suffix) and file name suffixes (_test.go, _linux.go)
  • Start an exported name with a capital letter and an unexported name with a lower-case letter. The case sets the visibility
  • Keep a name short when its scope is short: i, r, ctx. Use a longer name when the scope is long
  • Write an acronym in one case: HTTPClient, userID, parseURL
  • Use one short lower-case word for a package name: orders, payment. Do not use underscores or camelCase
  • Do not repeat the package name in a name: orders.Service, not orders.OrdersService

Useful tips

  • Name a one-method interface after the method plus -er: Reader, Writer, Stringer
  • Do not put Get in front of a getter: Total(), not GetTotal(). A setter is SetTotal
  • Name an error value with Err first, and an error type with Error last: ErrNotFound, NotFoundError
  • Use gofmt for layout. Use a linter to enforce names: staticcheck (ST1003, ST1012) or revive (var-naming)

General anti-patterns

  • snake_case and SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE: max_retry_count, MAX_RETRY_COUNT
  • A package name that repeats its folder path or is too generic: util, common, helpers
  • A package name that says nothing: models, types, base
  • An I prefix on an interface: IOrderRepository

docs.text: Kind Rule Examples Why this name Exported function MixedCaps, first letter capital CalculateTotal, NewOrder A capital letter exports the name. docs.title: Acronyms and initialisms
docs.text:
A word that is an acronym keeps one case in the whole name.

Bad Better Why HttpClient HTTPClient An initialism is all capitals. userId userID Same rule. ParseUrl ParseURL Same rule. xmlHttpRequest xmlHTTPRequest In an unexported name, the first word stays lower case. ServeHttp ServeHTTP The standard library writes ServeHTTP.

Conflict: the Go rule is the opposite of the Java rule (HttpClient). The Go code review comments give examples: URL or url but not Url, and appID but not appId. The common initialisms (API, ASCII, HTML, HTTP, ID, JSON, URL, UTF8) are listed in the golint source and in staticcheck ST1003. Id and Ok are not special: Go writes ID, and ok is a normal word in lower case.

docs.text: Good Bad Why orders ordersPackage, orders_pkg The Go blog: a package name is lower case, with no under_scores or mixedCaps. orderstore order_store, orderStore The Go blog: one lower-case word, no separators. payment common, util, helpers The Go blog: a package name says what the package provides. orders.Service orders.OrdersService The caller already writes orders., so the type name need not repeat it. orders.New orders.NewOrders The same rule applies to a constructor.

docs.text:
These patterns come from the standard library. They are practice, not rules of a style guide.

docs.title: Java and Kotlin
docs.text:
General patterns

  • Use camelCase for variables, parameters, methods and properties: orderTotal, findOrders
  • Use PascalCase for classes, interfaces, enums and annotations: OrderService, PaymentGateway
  • Use SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE for constants: MAX_RETRY_COUNT
  • Use all lower case for packages: com.example.shop.orders. Java forbids underscores. The Kotlin conventions only discourage them
  • Use a verb first for methods and a noun for values, as in the action and context pattern

Useful tips

  • Treat an acronym as a word in Java: HttpClient, XmlParser, userId. Kotlin keeps a two-letter acronym in capitals: IOStream
  • Do not put I in front of an interface and do not put Impl behind a class when a better name exists: OrderRepository and JpaOrderRepository, not IOrderRepository and OrderRepositoryImpl
  • Use a formatter and a checker to enforce the rules (Checkstyle or Spotless for Java, ktlint or detekt for Kotlin)

General anti-patterns

  • Hungarian notation: strName, lstItems
  • get and set prefixes on Kotlin properties: write val total, not fun getTotal()
  • Underscores in method names outside tests: calculate_total(). The Google Java guide allows underscores in test method names
  • A boolean that is not a statement: status, flag, check

Both languages run on the JVM and call each other, so a shared style is useful. The sections below mark what only one language does.

docs.title: JavaScript and TypeScript
docs.text:
General patterns

  • Use camelCase for variables, functions, methods and properties: orderTotal, fetchOrders
  • Use PascalCase for classes, interfaces, type aliases, enums and React components: OrderService, OrderSummary
  • Use SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE for module-level constants that never change: MAX_RETRY_COUNT
  • Use a verb first for functions and a noun for values, as in the action and context pattern
  • Treat an acronym as a word: userId, HttpClient, parseXml

Useful tips

  • Pick one style for file names and keep it: kebab-case.ts works on every file system. The Google guide asks for lower case with - or _
  • Do not put I in front of an interface, and do not put Type or Interface behind it: OrderRepository, not IOrderRepository
  • Use a formatter and a linter (ESLint with @typescript-eslint/naming-convention) to enforce the rules

General anti-patterns

  • Hungarian notation: strName, arrItems, objUser
  • A leading underscore for a private member in new code. Use the private keyword, or #field in plain JavaScript
  • Names that repeat the type: userObject, ordersArray
  • A boolean that is not a statement: status, flag, check

The JavaScript rules also apply to TypeScript. The sections below mark what is only TypeScript. Where a rule comes from community practice and not from a style guide, the text says so.

docs.title: Rust
docs.text:
General patterns

  • Use snake_case for functions, methods, variables and modules: calculate_total, order_total. Crate names may use snake_case or kebab-case
  • Use UpperCamelCase for types, traits and enum variants: OrderService, PaymentGateway, OrderStatus::Pending
  • Use SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE for constants and statics: MAX_RETRY_COUNT
  • Treat an acronym as a word in UpperCamelCase: Uuid, HttpClient, Json. In snake_case, write it in lower case: parse_json
  • Use lower case for a lifetime, and keep it short: 'a, 'de
  • Use a verb first for functions, as in the action and context pattern

Useful tips

  • Run cargo clippy. The compiler (rustc) warns about names that break the case rules (non_snake_case, non_camel_case_types, non_upper_case_globals)
  • Do not put get_ in front of a getter: total(), not get_total(). The Rust API guidelines give this rule
  • Name a conversion for its cost: as_ is free, to_ has a cost, into_ takes ownership
  • Name an error type in verb-object-error order: ParseIntError, not IntParseError. The API guidelines give this rule

General anti-patterns

  • camelCase for functions: calculateTotal
  • get_ on a plain getter: get_total()
  • A -rs or -rust suffix on a crate name: orders-rs
  • An I prefix on a trait: IOrderRepository

docs.title: Naming patterns
docs.text:
Patterns work across languages. Learn the pattern once, then use it for variables, functions, columns, endpoints and events.

General patterns

  • Order the words as action, high context, low context: get_user_messages. See Action and context.
  • Use one verb for one operation across the code base: get_order, get_invoice, get_refund.
  • Use two to four words per name: order_total_price, not total, and not the_total_price_of_the_order_after_tax.
  • Prefer full words over abbreviations: customer_id, not cust_id. See Abbreviations.
  • Name a boolean as a statement that is true or false: is_paid, has_discount, can_cancel, should_retry.
  • Put the unit in the name when the type does not carry it: timeout_seconds, amount_cents.

Useful tips

  • Use the glossary to choose a verb, a noun or a suffix.
  • Check a name with three questions: Does it say what the code does? Does it say to what? Can a new reader guess it?
  • Review names in code review. A bad name costs more than a bad line.

General anti-patterns

  • Generic names: data, info, item, handle_stuff()
  • Names with and: validate_and_save_order() → validate_order() and save_order()
  • Names that differ by one letter: order_item and orders_item
  • Mixed words for one idea: customer, client and user for the same actor

docs.title: Action and context
docs.text:
A good name answers two questions: what does the code do, and to what? This page shows how to order the words so the answer is clear.

General patterns

  • Use the A/HC/LC order: action, high context, low context. get_user_messages() reads as "get (action) the user (high context) messages (low context)".
  • Start with the verb in functions and methods: cancel_order(), apply_discount_code(), send_receipt_email().
  • Put the broad word before the narrow word: shipping_address_city, payment_retry_count.
  • Make names S-I-D: short, intuitive and descriptive. get_open_orders() passes. g_oo() is short but not intuitive. get_all_orders_that_are_still_open_and_unpaid() is descriptive but not short.
  • Keep the high context equal to the thing the code works on. If the function changes an order, order is the high context: refund_order(), close_order().
  • In a boolean, put the subject before the state: is_order_valid(), is_cart_empty().
  • Read the name aloud. If it sounds odd, the word order is probably wrong.

Useful tips

  • Test a new name by swapping the context words. If the meaning changes, the order matters and you must choose with care: get_post_tags() is not get_tag_posts().
  • The module or class often gives the high context. Then drop it from the name: order.cancel(), not order.cancel_order().
  • Use one verb for one operation. This guide uses get_ for a cheap read of known data, find_ for a search that may return nothing, list_ for a collection, and calculate_ for a computed value. You can choose other verbs. Keep them the same in the whole code base. See the glossary.
  • For function rules in Python, see Functions.

General anti-patterns

  • Noun-first function names: order_cancel() → cancel_order()
  • Context in the wrong order: message_user_get() → get_user_message()
  • Long chains of context words: get_all_active_user_unread_messages_count() → user.count_unread_messages()
  • Words with no content: handle_data(), process_item(), do_stuff()
  • Mixed verbs for one operation: fetch_order(), retrieve_invoice(), get_refund() in one code base

docs.title: A/HC/LC pattern
docs.text:
The pattern is: prefix? + action + high context + low context?. The prefix and the low context are optional. The naming cheatsheet by kettanaito describes the pattern.

Name Prefix Action High context Low context get_user_messages get user messages get_order_total get order total calculate_cart_subtotal calculate cart subtotal apply_coupon apply coupon refund_payment_fee refund payment fee should_retry_payment should retry payment send_order_confirmation_email send order confirmation email

Where the pattern does not fit

  • A name with a prefix such as is_cart_empty or has_order_shipped has no action. The prefix takes its place: prefix, subject, state.
  • A filter sits next to the noun it filters. In cancel_pending_orders, the state pending filters orders. The form is action + filter + noun.
  • A compound noun such as promo_code stays together. Do not split it into two contexts.

docs.title: Short, intuitive, descriptive (S-I-D)
docs.text: Property Question Failing example Passing example Short Can you type and read it without effort? get_all_orders_that_are_still_open() get_open_orders() Intuitive Does it read naturally, like speech? order_total_get() get_order_total() Descriptive Does it show what the code does and what it does it to? handle_order() ship_order()

docs.title: Verb first
docs.text:
Start function and method names with a verb. The verb tells the reader what happens. The noun tells the reader what it happens to.

Bad Better Why order_cancel() cancel_order() Verb first reads as a command. cart_total() calculate_cart_total() A bare noun does not say if the code reads, computes or loads. email_receipt() send_receipt_email() email could be a noun or a verb. discount_apply(code) apply_discount(code) Verb first matches cancel_order() and refund_payment(). user_by_email() find_user_by_email() A bare noun does not say if the code searches, creates or loads. find tells the reader that the search can return nothing. stock_check(sku) is_in_stock(sku) A boolean check uses is_ or has_. invoice_pdf() render_invoice_pdf() The verb shows that the code does work.

Exception: some names are nouns on purpose. A class name is a noun (OrderCancellation), and a property is a noun (order.total).

docs.title: Context order
docs.text:
Put the broad context first and the narrow context last. In alphabetical lists and in editor autocomplete, related names then stay together.

Bad Better Why city_shipping_address shipping_address_city shipping_address_* names group in the editor. retry_count_payment payment_retry_count The owner (payment) comes before the detail. total_order_price order_total_price order_* names group together. date_created_order order_created_date Same owner prefix as order_updated_date. name_customer_first customer_first_name The reader finds all customer_* fields at once.

docs.title: Reordering changes the meaning
docs.text:
The same words in a different order can describe a different thing. The pairs below suit many-to-many data, where each side can have many of the other.

Name What it means Reordered name What the reordered name means get_post_tags() Return the tags of one post. get_tag_posts() Return the posts that carry one tag. get_user_roles() Return the roles of one user. get_role_users() Return the users that hold one role. list_order_items() List the items in one order. list_item_orders() List the orders that contain one item. get_product_categories() Return the categories of one product. get_category_products() Return the products in one category. count_cart_items() Count the items in one cart. count_item_carts() Count the carts that hold one item.

docs.title: shouldComponentUpdate and shouldUpdateComponent
docs.text:
React names a lifecycle method shouldComponentUpdate. The method sits on the component. It answers the question "should I update?" The component is the subject, so the name does not need to say which component.

This guide suggests a convention for the two word orders. English grammar and React do not require it.

Name Reads as Use it for shouldComponentUpdate "Should this component update?" The subject comes first, then the verb. A method on the thing that decides, with no argument. shouldUpdateComponent "Should (we) update this component?" The verb comes first, then the object. A function outside the component. The component is the argument.

In Python, with snake_case, the same two forms are:

Method on the owner Function outside the owner order.should_ship() should_ship_order(order) cart.is_expired() is_cart_expired(cart) payment.can_retry() can_retry_payment(payment) subscription.should_renew() should_renew_subscription(subscription)

Both orders are valid. Choose by where the code lives, and keep one choice in the whole code base. The React name is an older exception to the verb-first rule. Other languages use camelCase for these names (shouldComponentUpdate). Python uses snake_case (should_update_component).

docs.text: Context Pattern Examples CRUD on a resource <verb>_<resource> create_order, update_shipping_address, delete_expired_carts Query by key find_<resource>_by_<key> find_user_by_email, find_product_by_sku Query many list_<filter>_<resources> list_open_orders, list_active_discounts Compute calculate_<owner>_<value> calculate_order_total, calculate_cart_tax Side effect <verb>_<owner> refund_payment, dispatch_order, cancel_subscription Boolean is_/has_/should_<owner>_<state>, can_<action>_<owner> is_cart_empty, has_order_shipped, can_cancel_order Event handler on_<owner>_<event> on_order_created, on_payment_failed Converter <source>_to_<target> order_to_invoice, cents_to_decimal

docs.text: Bad Better Why data_get() get_customer_profile() Verb first, and data says nothing. Use this when the function returns a customer profile. process_order_and_send_email() charge_order() and send_order_email() and in a name often hides two jobs. Split them. get_all_the_active_orders_for_user() list_user_active_orders() Remove filler words. Keep the context order. handle_cart() merge_guest_cart() handle hides the action. Use this when the function merges a guest cart into a user cart. payment_user_id payer_id One precise word replaces a chain. Use this when the user is the payer. get_user_data_list() list_users() list already says that the result is a collection, and data is filler. Use this when the function returns users. send_email_user() send_email_to_user() Without to, the reader cannot tell what is sent and what receives it.

docs.title: Booleans, collections, units and time
docs.text:
Four small decisions appear in almost every code base: how to name a flag, a group of things, a number with a unit, and a moment in time. This page gives a pattern for each one, with examples in Python, SQL, TypeScript and Go. A table of verb families at the end helps you to choose one verb per operation.

General patterns

  • Name a boolean as a statement that is true or false: is_paid, has_discount, can_cancel, should_retry, must_verify, was_refunded.
  • Use the positive form: is_enabled, not is_not_disabled.
  • Name a collection in the plural: orders, line_items. Name a map <value>_by_<key>: orders_by_id.
  • Name a count <thing>_count: order_count, retry_count.
  • Put the unit in the name when the type does not carry it: timeout_seconds, amount_cents, file_size_bytes.
  • Store money as integer minor units plus a currency code: order_total_cents and currency_code. _cents fits currencies with 100 minor units. For others, use _minor_units.
  • End a timestamp with _at and a date with _on or _date: paid_at, delivered_on.

Useful tips

  • Read the boolean in an if: if order.is_paid: reads like speech. if order.paid_flag: does not.
  • Some languages and style guides choose other forms. Swift asks that a boolean reads as an assertion about the receiver, such as x.isEmpty or a.intersects(b), and does not require a prefix for verb forms. .NET recommends an affirmative name and makes the Is/Can/Has prefix optional. See Swift API Design Guidelines and Names of type members. This guide uses the is_/has_/can_/should_ family as the project convention, not as a universal law.
  • If a language type carries the unit (timedelta, time.Duration), do not repeat the unit in the name.
  • For function names with the same prefixes, see Functions. For variable rules, see Variables. For column rules, see Columns.

General anti-patterns

  • Flags: paid_flag, discount_flag → is_paid, has_discount
  • Negative booleans: is_not_active, disable_cache = False → is_active, is_cache_enabled = True
  • A singular name for a collection: order = get_open_orders() → orders = get_open_orders()
  • A bare number for a duration: timeout = 30 → timeout_seconds = 30
  • A float for money: price = 19.99 → price_cents = 1999
  • A timestamp with no zone information: created = now() → created_at = now(tz=UTC)

docs.title: Prefixes
docs.text:
Prefix Use it for Python TypeScript SQL Go is_ A state is_paid isPaid is_paid isPaid has_ Owning something has_discount hasDiscount has_discount hasDiscount can_ Permission or ability can_cancel canCancel can_cancel canCancel should_ A decision or advice should_retry shouldRetry should_retry shouldRetry must_ A requirement must_verify_email mustVerifyEmail must_verify_email mustVerifyEmail was_ A past fact was_refunded wasRefunded was_refunded wasRefunded will_ A planned future fact will_renew willRenew will_renew willRenew allows_ Permission granted by the object allows_guest_checkout allowsGuestCheckout allows_guest_checkout allowsGuestCheckout

In Go, a name that starts a field in an exported struct begins with a capital letter: IsPaid. A local variable uses isPaid.

docs.title: Bad → better
docs.text: Bad Better Why paid_flag is_paid flag says the type, not the meaning. status_ok is_status_ok The prefix marks a boolean and reads as a statement in an if. is_not_disabled is_enabled Double negatives make readers stop and think. disable_notifications = False should_send_notifications = True A negative name with False becomes a double negative. no_discount has_discount State the fact in the positive form. discount (as a boolean) has_discount A noun can be an amount, a code or a flag. check_stock (as a field) should_check_stock A verb alone reads as an action, not as a value. cart_empty() is_cart_empty() The prefix tells the reader the result is a boolean. valid is_valid A bare adjective hides the type. guest is_guest guest could be a user object. order.refund order.was_refunded The prefix shows a fact about the past. email_verified_boolean is_email_verified Never put the type in the name.

docs.title: Patterns
docs.text:
Pattern Rule Python TypeScript SQL Go List Plural noun orders orders orders orders Map <value>_by_<key> orders_by_id ordersById n/a (a table keyed by id) ordersByID Unique values unique_<items> unique_skus uniqueSkus n/a (use DISTINCT) uniqueSKUs Count <thing>_count order_count orderCount order_count orderCount Sum of money <owner>_total_<value> order_total_cents orderTotalCents order_total_cents orderTotalCents Index <thing>_index item_index itemIndex item_index itemIndex Id list <thing>_ids order_ids orderIds order_ids orderIDs Batch <thing>_batch order_batch orderBatch order_batch orderBatch Page <thing>_page order_page orderPage order_page orderPage

Id casing

Go style writes initialisms in capitals: orderID, orderIDs. Python and SQL use lower case. TypeScript commonly writes orderId.

docs.title: Bad → better
docs.text:
Bad Better Why order_list orders The plural already says that it is a collection. orders (one order) order A plural name for one object misleads. order_dict orders_by_id by_id states the key. The type is not in the name. orders_map orders_by_id A map without a key name hides how to look up. num_orders order_count num can mean "number" or "numeric". orders_len order_count len is a function name, not a domain word. count retry_count A bare count does not say what is counted. i (index of an item) item_index One-letter names are fine only in tiny loops. id_list order_ids The name says what the ids belong to. data order_summary data fits any variable. Use a name that says what the data is. total (number of rows) row_count total can also be a money sum. Count with _count. items_array line_items Never put the type in the name.

Count or total?

order_count is the number of orders. order_total_cents is a sum of money for an order. Do not mix the two.

docs.title: Units in names
docs.text:
Quantity Name Unit Why Timeout timeout_seconds seconds No guess about seconds or milliseconds. Retry delay retry_delay_ms milliseconds The short form ms is common and clear. Cache lifetime cache_ttl_seconds seconds TTL needs a unit. File size file_size_bytes bytes size alone could be KB or MB. Upload limit upload_max_megabytes megabytes mb could mean megabytes or megabits. Distance distance_km kilometres Avoids a mix of miles and km. Weight package_weight_grams grams Shipping systems often use grams or ounces. Temperature temperature_celsius °C Kelvin and Fahrenheit also exist. Rate limit requests_per_minute per minute The period is part of the meaning. Bandwidth bandwidth_mbps megabits per second Avoids confusion with megabytes.

Unit symbols

Standard unit symbols such as ms, km and mbps, and standard acronyms such as ttl, are exceptions to the full-words rule. Write them in lower case. Spell out a unit when two readings are possible.

docs.title: Money
docs.text:
Store money as an integer amount in minor units, with an ISO 4217 currency code. Floating-point numbers cannot store 0.1 exactly. The ISO 20022 message definitions pair every amount with a currency code. ISO 20022 uses decimal amounts in major units, so convert at the system boundary. ISO 4217 defines the codes and the number of minor-unit digits.

Concept Name Example value Why Total in minor units order_total_cents 1999 Integers avoid rounding errors. Currency currency_code "EUR" Use the three-letter ISO 4217 code. Tax tax_amount_cents 320 Same unit as the total. Discount discount_amount_cents 500 discount alone could be a percent. Refund refunded_amount_cents 1999 Past participle shows a fact. Exchange rate eur_to_usd_rate 1.0842 A rate between two currencies. Name the pair. Fee rate fee_rate 0.029 A ratio from 0 to 1. Rounding rounding_mode "half_even" Name the rule, not the code.

Use _cents only for currencies with 100 minor units. For currencies with another number of minor units, use _minor_units: order_total_minor_units.

docs.title: Ratios and percentages
docs.text:
In this guide, rate means a ratio. For events per period, put the period in the name: requests_per_minute.

Name Meaning Example value Why discount_rate Ratio from 0 to 1 0.15 rate says "ratio", not "percent". discount_percent Number from 0 to 100 15 percent states the scale. conversion_ratio Ratio of two counts 0.032 A ratio has no unit. error_rate Errors per request 0.001 Same scale as discount_rate. tax_basis_points Parts per 10,000 250 basis_points avoids decimals.

docs.title: Timestamps, dates and durations
docs.text: Concept Python SQL TypeScript Go Why Moment an event happened paid_at paid_at paidAt paidAt _at marks a timestamp. Moment in UTC created_at_utc created_at_utc createdAtUtc createdAtUTC State the zone when it is not obvious. Calendar date delivered_on delivered_on deliveredOn deliveredOn _on marks a date without a time. Birth date birth_date birth_date birthDate birthDate _date also works for a date. Duration session_duration_seconds session_duration_seconds sessionDurationSeconds sessionDuration (type time.Duration) The unit is in the name, unless the type carries it. Expiry moment expires_at expires_at expiresAt expiresAt Points to a moment. Time to live ttl_seconds ttl_seconds ttlSeconds ttl (type time.Duration) Duration, not a moment. Start and end starts_at, ends_at starts_at, ends_at startsAt, endsAt startsAt, endsAt A matching pair.

docs.title: Bad → better
docs.text:
Bad Better Why timeout = 30 timeout_seconds = 30 The reader does not need to open the docs. created created_at created could be a boolean or an object. date (timestamp) occurred_at A timestamp is not a date. Use a verb in the past tense that fits the event. delivery_time (a date) delivered_on time could be a duration. ttl = 3600 ttl_seconds = 3600 A unit removes the guess. price = 19.99 price_cents = 1999 Integer money avoids rounding errors. amount amount_cents A bare amount hides the unit. tax = 0.2 tax_rate = 0.2 tax could be an amount. expiry expires_at A noun does not say if it is a date or a duration. created_at (naive local time) created_at stored as UTC, or created_at_local A name may claim UTC only if the value is UTC. Convert first, or say local. retry_interval = 5 retry_interval_seconds = 5 A bare number hides the unit. size file_size_bytes size has many meanings.

Metrics use base units

Prometheus recommends base units without prefixes: seconds, bytes and meters. A metric name ends with the unit, for example http_request_duration_seconds. See Prometheus naming practices.

docs.title: Verb families
docs.text:
Use this table to choose one verb per operation. Keep the same verb in the whole code base. See the glossary.

Verb Meaning Example 1 Example 2 Example 3 get Read known data cheaply get_order get_user_email get_order_total find Search, may return nothing find_user_by_email find_product_by_sku find_open_cart list Return a collection list_open_orders list_active_coupons list_user_addresses calculate Compute a value calculate_cart_subtotal calculate_cart_tax calculate_shipping_cost create Make a new record create_order create_refund create_shipment update Change a record update_shipping_address update_cart_item update_payment_method delete Remove a record delete_expired_carts delete_draft_order delete_saved_card validate Check without changing validate_coupon validate_address validate_order send Cause a message to go out send_receipt_email send_shipping_notice send_payment_reminder cancel Stop a process cancel_order cancel_subscription cancel_shipment

docs.title: Bad → better cookbook
docs.text:
A catalogue of common weak names and better replacements, grouped by category. Each row says why the new name is better. Use the page as a checklist during code review. Event names use the dotted form (order.created) for brokers and topics. In code, the same event is order_created or on_order_created.

General patterns

  • Name what the thing is or does, not its type: orders, not order_list.
  • Put the unit, the zone or the key in the name when the type does not carry it: timeout_seconds, created_at_utc, orders_by_id.
  • Use one word for one idea in the whole code base.
  • Prefer a name that a new teammate can guess without reading the code.

Useful tips

  • The better names are examples. A better name depends on what the code really does. Check that the replacement is true for your code before you rename. Where a row says "if", the condition is required.
  • Rename in small steps. Rename first, then change behaviour in a separate commit.
  • The pattern pages give the rule behind each row. This page gives only the fast answer.

General anti-patterns

  • Renaming only the variable and leaving the old word in the docs, the tests and the logs.
  • Adding a comment instead of fixing the name: d = 30 # days → retention_days = 30.

docs.title: Abbreviations
docs.text:
See Abbreviations.

Bad Better Why cust_id customer_id The reader should not need to guess the word. calc_ttl_amt() calculate_total_amount() Three abbreviations in one name hide the meaning. addr_ln1 address_line_1 The full words cost little and stay readable. pmt_mthd payment_method Vowel-dropping hurts search and speech. ord_dt ordered_on (if it holds a date only) or ordered_at (if it holds a time) dt could be date or datetime. _on marks a date. _at marks a timestamp. UsrRepo UserRepository A class name is read often. Spell it out.

docs.title: Generic names
docs.text: Bad Better Why data (if it holds an order summary) order_summary data fits any variable. info shipping_details Say what the information is about. process() capture_payment() process hides the action. handle_item(item) (if it packs the item) pack_item(item) Name the step, not the act of dealing with it. tmp (if it holds unpaid orders) unpaid_orders A temporary value still has a meaning. result (if it holds a refund receipt) refund_receipt result says nothing about content. OrderManager (if it schedules orders) OrderScheduler Manager hides the job. Name the class after the job.

docs.title: Misleading names
docs.text: Bad Better Why is_valid() that also saves the order validate_order() and save_order() A check must not change state. get_total() that changes the cart recalculate_cart_total() get suggests a read with no side effect. orders_list that is a dict orders_by_id The type and the name disagree. user_email that holds a user object user The name promises a string. delete_cart() that only archives archive_cart() The name must match what happens. discount_percent = 0.15 discount_rate = 0.15 percent suggests the scale 0 to 100. remaining_days that holds seconds remaining_seconds A wrong unit causes silent defects.

docs.title: Booleans
docs.text:
See Booleans, collections, units and time and Negation and optionality.

Bad Better Why paid_flag is_paid flag says the type, not the meaning. disable_logging = False is_logging_enabled = True A negative name with False is a double negative. valid is_valid A bare adjective hides the type. discount (as a boolean) has_discount A noun can be an amount, a code or a flag. not_shipped is_shipped State the fact in the positive form. Invert the value: not_shipped = True becomes is_shipped = False. check_stock (as a field) should_check_stock A bare verb reads as an action.

docs.title: Collections
docs.text: Bad Better Why order_list orders The plural already says that it is a collection. order (a group of orders) orders A singular name for many objects misleads. num_items item_count num could mean "number" or "numeric". sku_to_qty_dict quantity_by_sku The name shows value and key. id_list order_ids The name says what the ids belong to. items_array line_items Do not put the type in the name.

docs.title: Units and time
docs.text:
See Booleans, collections, units and time.

Bad Better Why timeout = 30 timeout_seconds = 30 The reader does not need to open the docs. price = 19.99 price_cents = 1999 plus currency_code Integer money avoids rounding errors. _cents fits currencies with 100 minor units only. created created_at _at marks a timestamp. ttl = 3600 ttl_seconds = 3600 A unit removes the guess. size (if it holds a file size) file_size_bytes size has many meanings. discount = 0.2 (if it is a ratio) discount_rate = 0.2 A ratio needs a clear word. If it is an amount, use discount_amount_cents.

docs.title: Functions
docs.text:
See Functions and Action and context.

Bad Better Why order_cancel() cancel_order() Verb first reads as a command. check_stock(sku) returning a boolean is_in_stock(sku) A boolean function uses is_, has_, can_ or should_. do_checkout() complete_checkout() do adds no meaning. get_and_save_user() get_user() and save_user() and often hides two jobs. email(order) send_order_email(order) email could be a noun or a verb. user_by_email() find_user_by_email() A bare noun does not say if the code searches, creates or loads.

docs.title: Classes
docs.text:
See Classes and Class methods.

Bad Better Why UserData (if it holds profile fields) UserProfile Data is filler. PaymentHelper (if it calls an external provider) PaymentGateway Helper hides the role. OrderUtil module order_rules with functions Stateless functions belong in a module, not in a class. AbstractBaseOrderFactoryImpl OrderFactory Remove layers of filler words. Order2 (if it is a frozen copy) OrderSnapshot A number does not say how the class differs. Exception1 PaymentDeclinedError The class name states the failure.

docs.title: Databases
docs.text:
See Tables, Columns, Indexes and Enums.

Bad Better Why tbl_order orders A table prefix repeats what the context shows. OrderID order_id PostgreSQL folds unquoted names to lower case, so mixed case needs quotes. fk_user user_id A foreign key column is <referenced_table_singular>_id. fk_ fits constraint names, not columns. is_deleted TINYINT deleted_at TIMESTAMP A timestamp says when. NULL says not deleted. idx1 idx_orders_customer_id The index name shows table and column. price FLOAT price_cents BIGINT Integer minor units avoid rounding errors.

docs.title: Tests
docs.text:
See Tests.

Bad Better Why test1() test_cancel_order_refunds_payment() The test name states the rule. test_order() test_create_order_rejects_empty_cart() One behaviour per test name. test_happy_path() test_checkout_succeeds_with_valid_card() Name the case, not the mood. test_error() test_checkout_fails_when_card_is_declined() The reader sees the cause and the result. test_it_works() test_apply_coupon_reduces_total() works is not a check.

docs.title: APIs
docs.text: Bad Better Why GET /getOrders GET /orders The HTTP method is the verb. POST /orders/create POST /orders Same reason. GET /order/{id} GET /orders/{id} Resources are plural nouns. GET /orders?customerID=7 GET /orders?customer_id=7 Pick one casing and use it everywhere. This guide uses snake_case. POST /orders/{id}/cancelOrder POST /orders/{id}:cancel Google AIP-136 style: a custom method as :verb. If your API does not follow AIP, use POST /orders/{id}/cancel. See Google AIP-136. {"error": 5} {"code": "PAYMENT_DECLINED"} A stable, readable code helps clients.

docs.title: Events
docs.text: Bad Better Why CreateOrder (as an event) order.created An event is a fact in the past. order_create_event order.created The word event repeats the context. OrderUpdate (if the address changed) order.address_changed Say what changed. payment (as a topic) topic payments with event types payment.captured and payment.refunded A topic holds a stream. Each event type inside it names one fact. issue_refund (as an event name) refund.issued A command is issue_refund. The event is the fact in the past.

docs.title: Metrics
docs.text: Bad Better Why requests http_requests_total A counter ends with _total. See Prometheus naming practices. latency_ms (as a metric name) http_request_duration_seconds Prometheus recommends base units. In code, _ms is fine. errors checkout_errors_total Say what fails. memoryUsage orderapp_memory_bytes One casing, an application prefix and an explicit unit. label user_id on a metric no user_id label A label with many values makes too many series.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text: Bad Better Why env Timeout PAYMENT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS By convention, environment variables are upper case, with a scope and a unit. DISABLE_EMAIL=false EMAIL_ENABLED=true Avoid a double negative. env db-url DATABASE_URL A shell variable name cannot contain a hyphen. Kubernetes name OrderService order-service Most Kubernetes object names are lower case with hyphens. See Kubernetes object names. flag new_checkout_flag_2 (if it turns on a new payment form) is_new_payment_form_enabled The name states the feature, reads as a boolean and needs no number.

docs.title: Negation and optionality
docs.text:
Names that say what is not true, or values that may be missing, cause many mistakes. This page shows how to write positive names, how to handle a name that you cannot change, and how to name a value that may be absent.

General patterns

  • Name the positive state: is_enabled, has_stock, is_active.
  • Make a flag mean "yes" when it is True: should_send_email = True, not skip_email = False.
  • Use one clear opposite word instead of a prefix: is_hidden instead of is_not_visible.
  • Name an optional value by its meaning, and show the optional type in the type system: middle_name: str | None.
  • Use NULL or None for "no value". Do not use -1, 0, "" or 9999-12-31 for it.
  • Use find_ when no result is a normal answer: find_coupon(). On other verbs, add _or_none or _or_default when the result can be missing: get_coupon_or_none(), get_setting_or_default().

Useful tips

  • Put the name in an if and read it aloud. if not order.is_not_paid takes two steps to read. if order.is_paid takes one.
  • A name that you cannot change comes from an outside standard. Keep it at the boundary and wrap it with a positive name inside your code. See the section "Names from outside".
  • A negative name is fine when the negative is the normal word in the domain: non_refundable, unsubscribed, offline.
  • For the prefixes that start a good boolean, see Booleans, collections, units and time.

General anti-patterns

  • Double negatives: if not is_not_ready: → if is_ready:
  • Inverted flags: disable_cache = False → is_cache_enabled = True
  • Negative prefixes that stack: is_non_inactive → is_active
  • Magic values for "missing": discount_cents = -1 → discount_cents = None
  • A function that returns None without saying so: get_coupon() → find_coupon()

docs.title: Double negatives and inverted flags
docs.text: Bad Better Why is_not_disabled is_enabled Two negatives mean one positive. not is_invalid is_valid The reader does not need to flip the meaning. disable_cache = False is_cache_enabled = True A negative name with False is a double negative. skip_validation = False should_validate = True The flag says what happens, not what is skipped. no_discount = False has_discount = True The positive form states the fact. is_not_empty (a cart or list) has_items The domain word states what the value holds. For a string, use is_empty with not. hide_banner = False is_banner_visible = True Use the state, not the command to change it. is_unavailable = False is_available = True Flip the name and the value together. The meaning stays the same. dont_retry = True should_retry = False A name with dont_ is hard to read in an if. The usual default is should_retry = True. ignore_case = False is_case_sensitive = True Names the state of the match. exclude_deleted = False should_include_deleted = True Use the positive of the pair. See Symmetry. non_active_users inactive_users One word for the opposite state.

docs.title: Negative prefixes
docs.text: Prefix Fine Use with care Why un- unsubscribed, unpaid is_not_unpaid Two negatives cancel each other and slow the reader. in- inactive, invalid is_not_inactive One negative is enough. non- non_refundable, non_taxable is_non_inactive A domain term that is negative by nature is fine. no_ the HTTP token no-cache, at the boundary no_discount_flag Prefer has_ for state. dis- disabled, disconnected (as domain terms) is_not_disabled In a boolean name, prefer is_enabled and is_connected.

docs.title: Names from outside
docs.text:
Some negative names come from a standard. Keep the exact name at the boundary and name your own variable in the positive form.

Outside name Where it comes from Inside name Why Cache-Control: no-cache HTTP header always_revalidate = True The header value is a standard token. must-revalidate and no-store are different directives. --no-verify Git flag should_run_hooks = False Keep the flag text in the command line only. The flag skips the commit hooks. --no-color CLI flag should_use_color = False The flag stays as the user types it. NOT NULL SQL constraint is_nullable = False The constraint is the storage rule. A required input is a separate rule: is_required. noindex HTML robots value is_indexing_allowed = False The HTML value stays as written.

docs.title: Missing, empty and unknown
docs.text:
Situation Name Value Why A value may be missing middle_name None / NULL Absence is not an empty string. A list is empty orders [] Return an empty list, not None. A value is unknown delivered_on NULL until delivery NULL says "not yet". A value does not apply company_name NULL for a person NULL says "not applicable". A value never expires expires_at NULL Do not use 9999-12-31. A limit does not exist upload_max_bytes None Do not use 0 or -1. A value exists but is empty note "" Only when an empty note is a real input.

NULL covers "missing", "not yet" and "not applicable". If a reader must tell them apart, add a status field or an enum.

docs.title: Names for optional results
docs.text: Bad Better Why get_coupon() that may return None find_coupon() find says that no result is a normal answer. If you keep get_, add _or_none. find_user() that raises get_user() find suggests that no result is a normal answer. See Action and context. get_setting() with a fallback get_setting_or_default() The fallback is part of the contract. try_parse_date() returning a flag parse_date_or_none() The name states what comes back. Change the return value too. lookup_discount() find_discount() One verb for a search. See Action and context. get_email() that may return "" get_email_or_none() An empty string is a value. Return None instead. user.phone = "" user.phone = None The empty string hides the missing value. discount_cents = -1 discount_cents = None A sentinel can leak into arithmetic. deleted = 0 / 1 deleted_at = NULL / timestamp The timestamp states when. NULL states not deleted. expires_at = '9999-12-31' expires_at = NULL A far date is a magic value. items_max = 0 (no limit) items_max = None 0 can also mean "none allowed". limit=-1 (all rows) limit=None The type shows that there is no limit.

docs.title: Language examples
docs.text: Language Optional field Why Python middle_name: str \| None The type states it (Python 3.10 or later, otherwise Optional[str]). TypeScript middleName?: string A question mark states that the field may be missing. Go MiddleName *string A pointer is a common idiom for an optional value. sql.NullString is another. SQL middle_name TEXT Columns accept NULL unless you add NOT NULL. Add it where a value must exist.
