docs.title: Command line
docs.text:
General patterns

  • Write a long option in lower case with hyphens: --output-format, --dry-run
  • Write a short option as one letter with one hyphen: -o, -v
  • Give each common option a long and a short form: -h and --help, -V and --version
  • Name a subcommand with a verb or a noun in lower case: init, build, config
  • Use the same word for the same thing in every command and in the environment: --timeout and SHOPCTL_TIMEOUT

Useful tips

  • Support --help and --version in every program. Print help to standard output and exit with code 0
  • Write a switch as a positive word (--color) and a negation with --no- (--no-color)
  • Put the unit in the name or the help text when a value has one: --timeout 30s, --max-size-bytes
  • Keep a long option short enough to type: two or three words at most

General anti-patterns

  • A single hyphen with a long name: -output (users read it as -o -u -t ...)
  • camelCase or snake_case in options: --outputFormat, --output_format
  • A negative switch with a negation: --no-disable-cache
  • Different words for one thing: --dir in one command and --folder in another
  • A subcommand that is a flag: --build

The examples use a command-line tool for an e-commerce shop called shopctl.

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Kind Rule Examples Why this name Long option -- and lower-case words with - --output-format, --dry-run The GNU long-option style. Hyphens make words easy to read. Short option - and one letter -o, -v, -n Fast to type. Short options joined - and several letters -abc means -a -b -c POSIX allows it. Option with a value --name value or --name=value --output-format json, --output-format=json Support both forms. Short option with a value -o value; -ovalue also works with getopt -o json, -ojson The separate form is the clear one. Switch (a flag with no value) an adjective or a verb --verbose, --force, --recursive The name states the effect, so the option needs no value. Negation --no-<name> --no-color, --no-cache A common style (not a GNU rule). Users know it from many tools. Repeated option the same option many times -v -v, --tag a --tag b Each use adds one value or one level. Option end marker -- shopctl run -- --not-an-option Everything after is an argument. Option with a unit the unit in the name or in the value --timeout 30s, --max-size-bytes 1048576 No guess about the unit. Option for a path --file, --dir, --config --config ./shop.toml The kind of path in the name. Option for a mode --mode, --output-format --output-format json A choice from a list. Option for a count --limit, --count, --max-<thing> --limit 50, --max-retries 3 The name says what the number counts. The environment name is SHOPCTL_MAX_RETRIES. See Configuration for its MAX rule. Option for time --since, --until, --timeout --since 2026-11-01, --timeout 30s --since and --until take a moment. --timeout takes a duration.

docs.title: Standard options
docs.text:
These options are common conventions. Many tools use them with the same meaning. Check the meaning in your own tool before you copy them.

Short Long Meaning Note -h --help Show help and exit. Exit code 0. POSIX has no -h, and GNU requires only --help. Some tools use -h for host or human-readable. -V --version Show the version and exit. Not a standard short form. Some tools use -v for version (docker, node). GNU requires only --version. -v --verbose Show more output. May repeat: -vv. -q --quiet Show less output. The opposite of verbose. -f --force Do not ask; overwrite. Dangerous. Document it. In kubectl, -f means --filename. -n --dry-run Show what would happen; do nothing. As in make -n. Not a standard: kubectl -n means namespace, and aws s3 spells it --dryrun. -r, -R --recursive Include subfolders. The case varies by tool. -o --output-format The output format. Some tools use -o and --output for an output file. -i --input The input file. -y --yes Answer yes to all questions. For scripts. --json Print the result as JSON. A common switch. --no-color Turn off color. See also the NO_COLOR variable. --config The path of a config file. --debug Show internal details.

docs.title: Subcommands
docs.text:
Pattern Rule Examples Why this name Command, then subcommand <tool> <noun> <verb> shopctl order list, shopctl order cancel 123 Group by the thing. Command, then verb <tool> <verb> <noun> shopctl list orders, shopctl cancel order 123 Group by the action. Standard verbs list, get, create, update, delete shopctl customer create The same set as in a REST API. Setup init, login, logout, config shopctl login Short and common. Info version, status, help shopctl status Common. Alias a short form of a command shopctl ls for list Document the main name. Plural or singular choose one shopctl orders list or shopctl order list Do not mix. Plugin <tool>-<name> on the path shopctl-export Git style: git-lfs.

Two styles: some tools put the noun first (gh pr list, aws s3 cp, docker container ls). Others put the verb first (kubectl get pods, git commit, docker run). Choose one and keep it in the whole tool.

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: Kind Rule Examples Why this name Positional argument a noun in upper case in help (common style) shopctl order get ORDER_ID The help shows the kind. Optional argument in square brackets in help [PATH] The usual help style. Many arguments three dots FILE... One or more. Choice braces in help {json,yaml,table} A list of allowed values. Default stated in help --limit N (default: 50) No guess.

docs.title: Environment variables and config
docs.text:
Source Rule Examples Why this name Environment variable for an option the tool name, then the option, in capitals SHOPCTL_OUTPUT_FORMAT for --output-format The same word in three places. The tool name is the <APP> prefix. Config file key the option name without -- output-format = "json" Match the option. Order of priority flag, then environment, then config, then default --output-format json wins over SHOPCTL_OUTPUT_FORMAT A common rule: the nearest source to the user wins. NO_COLOR a community standard NO_COLOR=1 Turns off color when set and not empty (no-color.org). Conventional names HOME, EDITOR, PAGER, TERM EDITOR=vim HOME and TERM are in POSIX. EDITOR and PAGER are Unix convention.

For the names of environment variables, see Configuration.

docs.title: Exit codes
docs.text: Code Meaning Note 0 Success 1 A general error 2 A wrong use of the command Common for a bad option. 126, 127 The shell could not run or find the command Set by the shell. Do not use them for the errors of your own tool. 130 Stopped by Ctrl-C 128 plus signal 2.

docs.title: Bad → better
docs.text:
Bad Better Why -output --output-format or -o One hyphen is for a one-letter option. --outputFormat --output-format Long options use hyphens. --output_format --output-format Same rule. --disable-cache --no-cache The --no- style is common, and the name of the switch stays positive (--cache). --nocolor --no-color Hyphen before color. --folder and --dir in one tool --dir everywhere One word for one thing. --build shopctl build An action is a subcommand. -help -h, --help A single hyphen reads as -h -e -l -p. --timeout 30 --timeout 30s or --timeout-seconds 30 The unit is clear. --verbose=true --verbose A switch needs no value.

See also

  • Systems overview, Configuration and Naming patterns
  • POSIX utility conventions, GNU standards: command-line interfaces, Command Line Interface Guidelines, NO_COLOR

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
General patterns

  • Write an environment variable in SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE: DATABASE_URL, LOG_LEVEL
  • Start the name with the app or the area, then the setting: SHOP_DATABASE_URL, SHOP_PAYMENT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS
  • Put the unit at the end when a value has one: _SECONDS, _MS, _BYTES
  • Write a boolean as a positive word and accept clear values: FEATURE_X_ENABLED=true
  • Keep the secret out of the name and out of the value in the repository: name STRIPE_API_KEY, store the value in a secret store

Useful tips

  • Use the same word in the variable, in the config file and in the code: payment_timeout_seconds, PAYMENT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS
  • Use a prefix for each service in a shared environment, so names do not collide
  • Document the default value and the unit of each variable in one file
  • Use kebab-case for Kubernetes resource names and keys of labels

General anti-patterns

  • A name without a unit: TIMEOUT (seconds or milliseconds?)
  • A negative boolean: DISABLE_CACHE=false
  • A name that contains the value: USE_PG14
  • A secret value in a default or a name: DB_PASSWORD_DEFAULT=hunter2
  • A mixed style in one file: dbHost, DB_PORT

The examples use an e-commerce shop. For the case styles of the languages, see the Languages overview.

docs.title: Environment variables
docs.text:
Kind Pattern Examples Why this name Connection string <SERVICE>_URL DATABASE_URL, REDIS_URL One variable holds the whole address. Host and port <SERVICE>_HOST, <SERVICE>_PORT DB_HOST, DB_PORT When the parts are separate. Timeout <THING>_TIMEOUT_<UNIT> HTTP_TIMEOUT_SECONDS, DB_CONNECT_TIMEOUT_MS The unit is in the name. Size <THING>_MAX_<UNIT> UPLOAD_MAX_BYTES The unit is in the name, and MAX is after the thing as for counts. Count <THING>_COUNT, <THING>_MAX_<UNIT> RETRY_COUNT, CONNECTIONS_MAX A total, or a limit with the word MAX after the thing. Switch <FEATURE>_ENABLED CACHE_ENABLED, DEBUG_LOGGING_ENABLED A positive boolean. Mode <AREA>_MODE CACHE_MODE=read_through A choice from a list of behaviors. Level LOG_LEVEL LOG_LEVEL=info A common name. Environment (community practice) APP_ENV; NODE_ENV in Node NODE_ENV=production The deployment stage. Do not branch the code on it. Set each variable on its own (Twelve-Factor App). Path <THING>_DIR, <THING>_PATH, <THING>_FILE DATA_DIR, CONFIG_FILE The kind of path is in the name. Prefix for one app <APP>_<SETTING> SHOP_DATABASE_URL, SHOP_LOG_LEVEL Avoids a clash. Prefix for a framework the framework prefix SPRING_PROFILES_ACTIVE, DJANGO_SETTINGS_MODULE The framework reads them.

By POSIX convention, the names that utilities use are upper case, with digits and the underscore, and they do not start with a digit. POSIX keeps lower-case names for applications. Most projects still use upper case for application variables.

docs.title: Secrets
docs.text:
Kind Pattern Examples Why this name API key <SERVICE>_API_KEY STRIPE_API_KEY The service and the kind. Secret token <SERVICE>_TOKEN GITHUB_TOKEN A token for a service. Client secret <SERVICE>_CLIENT_SECRET OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET The OAuth name. Password <SERVICE>_PASSWORD DB_PASSWORD The service and the kind of secret. Signing key <PURPOSE>_SIGNING_KEY JWT_SIGNING_KEY The purpose of the key. Path to a secret file <NAME>_FILE DB_PASSWORD_FILE The variable holds a path. Official Docker images read the value from that file, for example /run/secrets/db_password. This is a community convention. Secret manager entry <app>/<name>; the store or the account sets the environment shop/stripe-api-key A path in a secret store, not an environment variable.

Do not put a secret value in an environment variable name, in a Git repository, or in a log.

docs.title: Kubernetes names
docs.text: Kind Rule Examples Why this name Resource name lower case, digits and -; start and end with a letter or a digit shop-orders, payment-gateway Most kinds use a DNS subdomain name (at most 253 characters, . allowed). Some kinds use a DNS label (at most 63 characters). A Service name must start with a letter. Namespace lower case with - shop-prod, shop-staging A DNS label. Label key prefix/name; the name part has at most 63 characters, begins and ends with a letter or a digit, and may hold -, _ and . app.kubernetes.io/name A prefix with a domain avoids a clash. The prefixes kubernetes.io/ and k8s.io/ are reserved. Recommended labels app.kubernetes.io/<field> app.kubernetes.io/name, app.kubernetes.io/version, app.kubernetes.io/component The standard set. Custom label company prefix shop.example.com/team Your domain as a prefix. Annotation key the same form as a label shop.example.com/owner Annotations are for tools. ConfigMap the app and the purpose shop-orders-config The app tells who reads it, and config tells what is inside. Secret the app and the kind shop-orders-db-credentials The app tells who reads it, and db-credentials tells what is inside. Do not put the value in the name. Environment variable in a pod SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE DATABASE_URL The same as other environments. Helm value key camelCase replicaCount, image.repository The Helm chart style.

docs.title: Config files
docs.text: Format Key style Examples Notes YAML for a service snake_case or camelCase, one style payment_timeout_seconds Match the language of the app. TOML no rule in the TOML spec; Cargo and pyproject.toml use kebab-case max-connections Match the tool that reads the file. JSON the style of the API maxConnections Match the API. Properties (Java) dotted lower case shop.payment.timeout-seconds Spring relaxed binding accepts several forms. .env file like environment variables DATABASE_URL=... Not in the repository when it holds secrets.

docs.title: Bad → better
docs.text:
Bad Better Why TIMEOUT HTTP_TIMEOUT_SECONDS The unit is in the name. DISABLE_CACHE CACHE_ENABLED A positive boolean. dbHost in an env file DB_HOST The environment style. PASS DB_PASSWORD PASS could mean password or passphrase, and it lacks the service. USE_PG14 DATABASE_URL The version is part of the value, not the name. prod_db_url DATABASE_URL The environment is set by the deployment, not the name. The Twelve-Factor App keeps each variable separate from named environments. MyApp as a Kubernetes name my-app Kubernetes names are lower case. app as a label that names the application app.kubernetes.io/name Use the standard key for the name of the application.

See also

  • Systems overview, Errors and Naming patterns
  • Kubernetes: labels and annotations, Recommended labels, The Twelve-Factor App: config

docs.title: Errors
docs.text:
General patterns

  • Give each error a stable code that a program can read: ORDER_NOT_FOUND, CARD_DECLINED
  • Write the code in SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE (AIP-193 asks for this in reason) or in lower_snake_case (Stripe uses card_declined). Use one style in the whole API
  • Name the thing and the problem: <RESOURCE>_<PROBLEM>
  • Keep a code the same for ever. Change the message, not the code
  • Write the message for a person and the code for a program

Useful tips

  • Use the HTTP status for the class of the error and the code for the exact reason: 404 with ORDER_NOT_FOUND
  • Name an exception class after the problem, with the suffix Error or Exception, as the language asks: OrderNotFoundError
  • Put the code, the message and the field in a fixed shape (see RFC 9457)
  • Keep a list of all codes in one file and in the documentation

General anti-patterns

  • A numeric code without a name: E1042
  • A code that is a sentence: THE_ORDER_WAS_NOT_FOUND_IN_DB
  • A code that leaks the implementation: NULL_POINTER, SQL_ERROR
  • One generic code for everything: ERROR, FAILED
  • A message that a program has to parse

The examples use an e-commerce shop. The name patterns below are community practice, except where the text names a standard. For field names inside the error body, see REST.

docs.title: Error code names
docs.text: Kind Pattern Examples Why this name Not found <RESOURCE>_NOT_FOUND ORDER_NOT_FOUND, CUSTOMER_NOT_FOUND The resource and the problem. Already exists <RESOURCE>_ALREADY_EXISTS COUPON_ALREADY_EXISTS The resource and the problem, as for NOT_FOUND. Invalid value INVALID_<FIELD> INVALID_EMAIL, INVALID_QUANTITY The field is in the name. Missing value MISSING_<FIELD> MISSING_CURRENCY_CODE The client sent nothing. Invalid means the client sent a wrong value. State conflict <RESOURCE>_<STATE> ORDER_ALREADY_SHIPPED, ORDER_NOT_CANCELLABLE The state that blocks the action. Permission PERMISSION_DENIED, UNAUTHENTICATED (gRPC status names) PERMISSION_DENIED These names are known to many clients. Limit <THING>_LIMIT_EXCEEDED RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED, CART_ITEM_LIMIT_EXCEEDED The limit and the fact. Payment PAYMENT_<PROBLEM> PAYMENT_DECLINED, PAYMENT_CARD_EXPIRED The thing first and the problem second, as in the other names. Dependency <SERVICE>_UNAVAILABLE PAYMENT_GATEWAY_UNAVAILABLE Says which service failed. Precondition FAILED_PRECONDITION (a gRPC status) FAILED_PRECONDITION The system is not in a state for this call. Internal INTERNAL (a gRPC status) INTERNAL A bug in the server. The client cannot fix it.

docs.title: HTTP status and code
docs.text:
The mapping follows the google.rpc.Code table. It is not a gRPC standard. The table also has 400 for FAILED_PRECONDITION and OUT_OF_RANGE, 499 for CANCELLED, and 504 for DEADLINE_EXCEEDED.

HTTP status gRPC code Example code Meaning 400 INVALID_ARGUMENT INVALID_EMAIL The request is wrong. 401 UNAUTHENTICATED TOKEN_EXPIRED The caller is not known. 403 PERMISSION_DENIED ORDER_ACCESS_DENIED The caller is known and not allowed. 404 NOT_FOUND ORDER_NOT_FOUND The resource does not exist. 409 ALREADY_EXISTS, ABORTED COUPON_ALREADY_EXISTS A conflict with the state. 422 no standard mapping QUANTITY_OUT_OF_RANGE The request is well formed but not valid. Many APIs use 400 instead. 429 RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED Too many requests. 500 INTERNAL INTERNAL A server bug. 503 UNAVAILABLE PAYMENT_GATEWAY_UNAVAILABLE A temporary failure.

docs.title: Error details (AIP-193)
docs.text: Google AIP-193 puts an ErrorInfo in an error. The reason is a stable UPPER_SNAKE_CASE code of at most 63 characters, such as ORDER_NOT_FOUND. The domain names the service that owns the reason, such as orders.shop.example.com. The metadata keys use lowerCamelCase.

docs.title: Problem details (RFC 9457)
docs.text:
RFC 9457 (which replaces RFC 7807) defines a JSON body for an HTTP error with standard member names.

Member Meaning Example type A URI that names the kind of problem. https://api.shop.example/problems/order-not-found title A short summary that does not change. Order not found status The HTTP status. It is advisory; the real status is in the response line. 404 detail An explanation for this case. Order 12345 does not exist. instance A URI reference for this one occurrence of the problem. /errors/9f2c7a41 code An extension: the stable code. ORDER_NOT_FOUND errors An extension: a list of field problems. [{ "field": "email", "code": "INVALID_EMAIL" }]

The media type is application/problem+json.

docs.title: Exception names
docs.text:
Language Pattern Examples Notes Python <Problem>Error OrderNotFoundError, InvalidCouponError PEP 8: use the suffix Error when the exception is an error. Java <Problem>Exception OrderNotFoundException The JDK names exceptions with the suffix Exception. C# <Problem>Exception OrderNotFoundException The .NET guidelines require the suffix. JavaScript, TypeScript <Problem>Error OrderNotFoundError The built-in classes end with Error (TypeError), and your class extends Error. Go Err<Problem> for a value, <Problem>Error for a type ErrNotFound, NotFoundError Effective Go and the standard library use both forms. Rust <Problem>Error and variants OrderError::NotFound The type ends with Error, so the variant names only the cause.

For the language rules, see the Languages overview.

docs.title: Bad → better
docs.text:
Bad Better Why E1042 ORDER_NOT_FOUND A name is readable. error INVALID_EMAIL A generic word says nothing. NULL_POINTER INTERNAL Do not leak the implementation. ORDER_NOT_FOUND_IN_DATABASE ORDER_NOT_FOUND The caller does not need to know about the database. Order not found as a code ORDER_NOT_FOUND A code is not a sentence. 404 only 404 plus ORDER_NOT_FOUND The status gives the class. The code gives the reason. orderError OrderNotFoundError The class names the problem. Failure PaymentDeclinedError Say what failed.

See also

  • Systems overview, REST and Configuration
  • RFC 9457, Google AIP-193: errors, gRPC status codes

docs.title: Events
docs.text:
General patterns

  • Name an event for a fact that already happened, in the past tense: OrderPlaced, PaymentCaptured
  • Name a command for a request in the imperative: PlaceOrder, CapturePayment
  • Name a topic for the stream of one kind of event, in lower case with a clear scope: shop.orders.v1
  • Use the same field names in an event as in the REST API and the database: order_id, customer_id
  • Put the metadata in an envelope and the data of the fact in the payload

Useful tips

  • Name an event for what the business sees, not for a row change: OrderShipped, not OrderRowUpdated
  • Add a version to the event type or the topic, so consumers can handle two versions at once
  • Use a timestamp in RFC 3339 form, in UTC. In the CloudEvents envelope the attribute is time. In a payload, a field such as occurred_at is fine
  • Use CloudEvents attribute names when the platform supports them

General anti-patterns

  • A name that says how the data changed instead of what happened: OrderUpdated, OrderChanged
  • One name for a command and an event: OrderPlaced for both a request and a fact
  • A topic that names the consumer: billing-service-input
  • A payload that has the whole database row

The examples use an e-commerce shop.

docs.title: Events and commands
docs.text: Kind Tense Examples Why this name Event past OrderPlaced, OrderShipped, PaymentCaptured A fact cannot be refused. Command imperative PlaceOrder, ShipOrder, CapturePayment A request can be refused. Query a question WhatIsOrderStatus Asks for data. Most systems use a request-response API for this, not a message. Failure event past, with the failure PaymentFailed, OrderRejected The fact is that it failed. Compensation event past PaymentRefunded, OrderCanceled The undo step is also a fact. Deadline event past OrderExpired, PaymentTimedOut Time passed.

docs.title: Event type names
docs.text:
Pattern Examples Notes <Aggregate><PastVerb> OrderPlaced, CustomerRegistered, InvoiceIssued A common form in domain-driven design (community practice). Reverse domain com.shop.order.placed CloudEvents recommends a reverse-DNS prefix for type. With a version com.shop.order.placed.v1, OrderPlacedV1 A version in the name or in the schema. Dotted lower case order.placed, payment.captured Used by webhooks, for example invoice.paid. Domain scope shipping.parcel.dispatched Adds the bounded context.

Conflict: some platforms use PascalCase names (OrderPlaced). Others use dotted lower case (order.placed). Choose one and use it in the whole company.

docs.title: Topic and queue names
docs.text:
Kafka and other brokers set no naming rules beyond the allowed characters. The patterns below are community practice. In Kafka, a topic name can mix . and _, but the two collide in metric names, so use one of them.

Kind Pattern Examples Why this name Topic <domain>.<entity>.<version> shop.orders.v1, shop.payments.v1 The scope and the version are in the name. Topic, by event <domain>.<entity>.<event> shop.orders.placed One topic for one event type. Dead-letter topic (community practice) the topic plus .dlq shop.orders.v1.dlq Where failed messages go. Retry topic (community practice) the topic plus .retry shop.orders.v1.retry Where messages wait for a new try. Queue <consumer>.<source> billing.orders-placed A queue belongs to its consumer. Consumer group the service name billing-service Names the reader. Environment prefix or the cluster, not both prod.shop.orders.v1 Do not repeat it in both places.

docs.title: Envelope fields
docs.text:
CloudEvents defines the names of the envelope. The table shows the required and common attributes.

Field Meaning Examples Why this name id An id that is unique within the source. evt_01HZ... Needed for de-duplication. source Where the event came from. /shop/orders A context for id. specversion The CloudEvents version. 1.0 Required by the standard. type The kind of event. com.shop.order.placed Consumers route by type. time When the event occurred (RFC 3339). 2026-11-07T10:15:00Z A timestamp. Use UTC by habit. RFC 3339 also allows an offset. subject The thing that the event is about. orders/12345 Narrows the source. datacontenttype The format of the data. application/json Tells how to read data. dataschema A link to the schema of the data. https://schemas.shop/order-placed/v1 Helps validation. data The payload. { "order_id": "12345" } The data of the fact. correlationid Links events of one flow. req_7d9a... A common extension (community practice). For tracing, the traceparent extension is the standard way. causationid The id of the cause. evt_01HY... A common extension (community practice).

The names of all CloudEvents attributes, including extensions, use only lower-case letters and digits, with no underscore. They should be at most 20 characters. The required attributes are id, source, specversion and type. The others are optional.

docs.title: Payload fields
docs.text: Kind Rule Examples Identifier <entity>_id order_id, customer_id Timestamp <event>_at placed_at, shipped_at Money an integer in minor units plus a currency code total_amount_cents, currency_code Status the new state, not the old status: "shipped" Previous value previous_<field> previous_status Items plural noun items

docs.title: Bad → better
docs.text:
Bad Better Why OrderUpdated OrderShipped The name tells what happened. PlaceOrderEvent OrderPlaced An event is a past fact; drop the type word. order_place PlaceOrder A command is a verb phrase in the imperative. topic1 shop.orders.v1 The scope and the version are in the name. billing-input shop.orders.v1 A topic is named for the data, not for the reader. ts time in the envelope; occurred_at in a payload A full word, as in CloudEvents. OrderCreatedV2 and OrderCreated in one topic OrderCreated with a versioned dataschema, or a new topic shop.orders.v2 Version the schema or the topic, not the event name. OrderPaid for a failed payment PaymentFailed Say what really happened.

See also

  • Systems overview, REST and GraphQL
  • CloudEvents specification, AsyncAPI

docs.title: Feature flags
docs.text:
General patterns

  • Name a flag for the feature it controls, not for the team or the ticket: checkout_one_click, not team_b_flag_2
  • Write a flag as a positive statement: new_checkout_enabled, not disable_old_checkout
  • Use one case style for all flags, and keep the style of the flag tool
  • Put the kind of flag in the name or in the tool: release, experiment, operations, permission
  • Give each flag an owner and a removal date

Useful tips

  • Use a prefix for the area when the project has many flags: checkout_, search_
  • Name the flag for the new behavior, so the code reads well: if flags.checkout_one_click:
  • Remove a release flag when the feature is fully on. A flag that stays for months is a hidden branch in the code
  • Use kill_switch in the name of an operations flag that turns off a risky part in an incident

General anti-patterns

  • A negative name: disable_cache, no_new_ui
  • A name with a ticket or a person: jira_1234, anna_test
  • A vague name: new_feature, flag1, test
  • A name with a version or a state in it: new_search_v2_on
  • A flag that is never removed

The examples use an e-commerce shop. No standard sets flag names. The OpenFeature specification only says that a flag key is a string. The patterns below are community practice. The four kinds of flag (release, experiment, operations, permission) come from Martin Fowler's article on feature toggles. For the same rules on environment variables, see Configuration.

docs.title: Names by kind
docs.text: Kind Pattern Examples Why this name Release flag <feature>_enabled or <feature> checkout_one_click_enabled, new_search_ranking Turns on a finished feature step by step. Experiment exp_<name>; choose this one form exp_cart_recommendations, exp_pricing_page The prefix marks a test that ends. Operations flag <area>_<behavior>_enabled payment_retry_enabled, search_cache_enabled Controls the load or the behavior of the system. Kill switch (practice) <area>_kill_switch recommendations_kill_switch, email_sending_kill_switch Turns a part off in an incident. Permission flag <capability>_allowed or <plan>_<feature> bulk_export_allowed, pro_reports Gives a feature to a group of users. Variant the name of the arm control, treatment, variant_a The values of an experiment. Percentage rollout (practice) the flag stays the same; the percent is data new_checkout_enabled at 10% Do not put the number in the name. Dark launch (practice) <feature>_dark or <feature>_shadow new_pricing_shadow Runs the code with no effect for the user. Migration flag (practice) migrate_<what> migrate_orders_to_new_db The flag ends with the migration.

docs.title: Flag lifecycle
docs.text: Stage Meaning Action Example Created The flag exists and is off. Name it, set an owner and a removal date. new_checkout_enabled Rolling out The flag is on for a part of the users. Watch the metrics. 5%, 25%, 100% Fully on The flag is on for all users. Remove the old code path. Removed The flag and the old code are gone. Delete the flag in the tool. Permanent An operations flag or a permission flag stays. Review it each quarter. payment_retry_enabled

docs.title: Flag metadata
docs.text: Field Meaning Example key The name that code uses. new_checkout_enabled description One sentence on what the flag does. Shows the one-click checkout button. owner The team or person who removes it. checkout-team kind The type of flag. release created_at When the flag was made. 2026-11-07 remove_by The date to remove it. 2026-12-31

docs.title: In the code
docs.text: Case Rule Examples Constant for a key Use the case of the language FLAG_NEW_CHECKOUT, flags.newCheckoutEnabled Call that reads a flag A boolean question; OpenFeature names it getBooleanValue is_enabled("new_checkout_enabled"), client.getBooleanValue("new_checkout_enabled", false) A branch Name the new path for what it does if new_checkout_enabled: render_one_click() A test Name the flag state test_checkout_with_one_click_enabled

docs.title: Bad → better
docs.text:
Bad Better Why disable_old_checkout new_checkout_enabled A positive name. flag1 checkout_one_click_enabled A name states the feature. jira_1234 checkout_one_click_enabled A ticket id says nothing about the feature. new_search_v2_on new_search_ranking A version number and on become wrong when the flag changes. The suffix _enabled is different: it names the question, and the flag value answers it. anna_test exp_cart_recommendations Name the test, not the person. use_new_db migrate_orders_to_new_db The flag is for a migration with an end. experiment exp_cart_recommendations A prefix and a subject. killswitch recommendations_kill_switch Say what it turns off.

See also

  • Systems overview, Observability and Configuration
  • OpenFeature specification, Martin Fowler: feature toggles

docs.title: GraphQL
docs.text:
General patterns

  • Use PascalCase for type names: Order, OrderStatus, CreateOrderInput
  • Use camelCase for fields, arguments and mutation fields: orderTotal, customerId, createOrder
  • Use SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE for enum values: PENDING, SHIPPED
  • Name a mutation with a verb first: createOrder, cancelOrder
  • Name a query field with a noun: order, orders
  • Give each mutation one input type and one payload type: CancelOrderInput, CancelOrderPayload. This is a GitHub-style convention

Useful tips

  • Name a field after what it is, not after where it comes from: customer, not customerFromCrm
  • Use the same word for the same thing in every type. id is an opaque global identifier of an object (Relay Node). The order_id of the REST API maps to orderId when a field needs the plain key
  • Return the changed object in the payload, so the client needs no second call
  • Use a linter, for example graphql-eslint with the naming-convention rule

General anti-patterns

  • A verb in a query: getOrder, fetchOrders
  • A type name with a noise suffix: OrderType, OrderObject
  • A mutation that returns only a boolean: cancelOrder: Boolean
  • Names with the version in them: OrderV2. Evolve the schema instead

The examples use an e-commerce shop.

docs.title: Names by kind
docs.text: Kind Rule Examples Why this name Object type PascalCase noun Order, Customer, OrderLine Apollo and the public GraphQL APIs use PascalCase. The spec only requires a valid name. Interface PascalCase noun or adjective Node, Timestamped An interface names a shape that many types share. Node is the Relay interface for objects with a global id. Union PascalCase noun for the choice SearchResult, PaymentMethod The name states what the member types have in common. Input type (Apollo and GitHub style) mutation name plus Input CreateOrderInput, CancelOrderInput Ties the input to its mutation. Payload type (Apollo and GitHub style) mutation name plus Payload CreateOrderPayload, CancelOrderPayload Ties the result to its mutation. Enum singular PascalCase noun OrderStatus, Currency One value is one status. Enum value SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE PENDING, PARTIALLY_SHIPPED The spec examples and Apollo use this style. Scalar PascalCase noun DateTime, Url A custom value type. For money, use an object: Money { amountCents currencyCode }. Field camelCase noun totalAmountCents, shippedAt The unit is in the name, as in the REST API and the database. Boolean field is, has plus a word isActive, hasGiftWrap A boolean reads as a statement. Timestamp field <event>At createdAt, shippedAt The same suffix as in the database and REST. List field plural noun items, orders A plural tells the client that the value is a list. Argument camelCase word first, after, status Arguments follow the field style. Relay fixes first, after, last and before. Query, one item singular noun order(id: ID!), customer(id: ID!) One object by id. Query, a list plural noun orders(first: Int), products A set of objects. Query, current user (community practice) viewer (GitHub, Relay) or me viewer, me An alias for the caller, so the client needs no id. Mutation verb plus noun (Shopify uses noun first: orderCancel) createOrder, cancelOrder, addOrderItem An action on a resource. Choose one order and keep it. Subscription (community practice) noun plus past event orderShipped, shipmentDelivered A stream of events. Use the event names from Events. Directive camelCase @deprecated, @specifiedBy The spec directives use lower camel case. Fragment the type plus a purpose OrderSummaryFields A client file may hold many fragments, so the name says the type and the use. Operation name (client side) PascalCase; a verb is fine here GetOrderDetails, CancelOrder It shows in logs and tools. The no-verb rule is for query fields, not for operation names.

docs.title: Mutations
docs.text: Pattern Rule Examples Create create plus a noun createOrder, createCustomer Update update plus a noun updateOrder, updateCustomer Delete delete plus a noun deleteAddress Action a verb plus a noun cancelOrder, shipOrder, refundPayment Add or remove from a list add or remove plus a noun addOrderItem, removeOrderItem One input input: <Mutation>Input! createOrder(input: CreateOrderInput!) Payload the changed object plus errors for the user (Shopify uses userErrors) { order { id } userErrors { field message } }

docs.title: Relay connections
docs.text:
The Relay specification defines paged lists. Its names are part of the contract.

Name Meaning Examples <Type>Connection The paged list. OrderConnection <Type>Edge One item and its cursor. OrderEdge edges The list of edges. orders { edges { node { id } } } node The item in an edge. edge.node cursor The position of an edge. edge.cursor pageInfo The paging data. PageInfo hasNextPage, hasPreviousPage Whether more items exist. pageInfo.hasNextPage startCursor, endCursor The first and last cursor. pageInfo.endCursor first, after Forward paging arguments. orders(first: 10, after: "abc") last, before Backward paging arguments. orders(last: 10, before: "abc") totalCount A common extra field. It is not part of the Relay specification. orders { totalCount }

docs.title: Bad → better
docs.text:
Bad Better Why getOrder order A query is a noun. OrderType Order The word Type repeats what the schema says. order_total orderTotal Fields use camelCase. pending as enum value PENDING Enum values use capitals. cancelOrder(id: ID!): Boolean cancelOrder(input: CancelOrderInput!): CancelOrderPayload! The client gets the changed order. OrderInput for create and update CreateOrderInput, UpdateOrderInput The inputs differ. orderList orders A plural noun is enough. isNotActive isActive A positive name. createdTime createdAt The same suffix as the other APIs.

See also

  • Systems overview, REST and Events
  • GraphQL specification, Relay connections, Apollo naming conventions

docs.title: Observability
docs.text:
General patterns

  • Name a metric for what it measures, with its unit as a suffix: http_request_duration_seconds
  • Use base units: seconds, bytes, ratios from 0 to 1. Do not use milliseconds or percent in the name of a metric
  • End a counter with _total: orders_placed_total
  • Use snake_case for metric names and label names (Prometheus). Use dotted lower case for OpenTelemetry names: http.server.request.duration
  • Keep the number of label values small. Never use a user id or a request id as a label

Useful tips

  • Put the name of the thing first and the unit last: memory_usage_bytes, payment_amount_total. A value with no unit has no unit suffix: queue_depth
  • Use the same label name for the same thing in every metric: status_code, not code in one and status in another
  • Name a span for the operation, not the data: GET /v1/orders/{order_id}, not GET /v1/orders/12345
  • Write log fields in one style and use the same names as in the API: order_id, customer_id

General anti-patterns

  • A unit that is not a base unit: request_duration_ms, memory_mb
  • A counter without _total: orders_placed
  • A high-cardinality label: user_id, email, request_id, a raw URL
  • A name with a per-service word in it: orders_service_http_requests_total (use a service label). One prefix for the whole application, such as shop_, is fine
  • A name with a type or a statistic in it: request_duration_histogram, avg_latency

The examples use an e-commerce shop. The metric rules come from the Prometheus naming guide and the OpenTelemetry semantic conventions. The label choices and the log field names are community practice.

docs.title: Metric names (Prometheus)
docs.text: Kind Pattern Examples Why this name Counter <thing>_<event>_total orders_placed_total, http_requests_total A counter only goes up, and _total says so. Counter with a unit <thing>_<unit>_total sent_bytes_total, processing_seconds_total The unit is before _total. Money is an exception to base units: use payment_amount_total with a currency label. Gauge <thing>_<unit> queue_depth, memory_usage_bytes A value that goes up and down. A value with no unit has no suffix. Info metric <thing>_info build_info Prometheus practice: a constant 1 with the data in labels. Gauge for a state (community practice) <thing>_state circuit_breaker_state A state with labels. Histogram <thing>_<unit> http_request_duration_seconds, response_size_bytes The buckets use the base unit. Ratio <thing>_ratio cache_hit_ratio A value from 0 to 1. Timestamp <thing>_timestamp_seconds last_success_timestamp_seconds Unix time in seconds. Process metric process_<thing> process_cpu_seconds_total The Prometheus client libraries export these standard names, so dashboards work with no change. Application prefix <app>_<thing> shop_orders_placed_total One prefix for the whole application.

docs.title: Labels
docs.text:
Label Meaning Examples Why this name method The HTTP method. GET, POST The same word as in HTTP. The set of values is small. route The route template, not the path. /v1/orders/{order_id} The template has few values. The raw path has many. status_code The HTTP status. 200, 404 The same word as in HTTP. The set of values is small. service The service that sent the data. orders, payments Better than a prefix. env The environment. prod, staging Set by the platform. result The outcome. success, error A short word for a choice with two or three values. error_code A stable error code, the reason of Errors. OpenTelemetry uses error.type. PAYMENT_DECLINED The same value as in the error body.

Do not use as a label: user_id, email, order_id, request_id, a full URL, a free-text message.

docs.title: OpenTelemetry names
docs.text:
Kind Pattern Examples Why this name Metric dotted lower case, a namespace first http.server.request.duration, db.client.operation.duration The semantic conventions use dotted names. Metric unit in the metadata, not the name unit s, unit By The name has no unit suffix. Attribute dotted lower case, a namespace first http.request.method, http.response.status_code, db.system.name A shared vocabulary. Custom attribute your domain as a namespace shop.order.id, shop.customer.tier Avoids a clash with the standard names. Span name HTTP server span: {method} {http.route}, or {method} alone with no route; database span: {db.operation.name} {target} GET /v1/orders/{order_id}, SELECT orders Few distinct names. Resource attribute service.name, service.version service.name=shop-orders Names the source of the data.

Conflict: Prometheus writes http_request_duration_seconds. OpenTelemetry writes http.server.request.duration with the unit in the metadata. When OpenTelemetry data goes to Prometheus, the dots become underscores, the unit becomes a suffix and a monotonic counter gets _total: http_server_request_duration_seconds. Attribute names change too: http.request.method becomes http_request_method. The translation can be configured, and newer versions can keep the dotted names.

docs.title: Log fields
docs.text:
Field Meaning Examples Why this name timestamp When the log line was made. 2026-11-07T10:15:00Z A common name. The OpenTelemetry log data model calls it Timestamp. level The severity. info, error A common name. OpenTelemetry calls it SeverityText. message The text for a person. Order placed A common name. OpenTelemetry calls it Body. logger The name of the source. shop.orders.service The module or class. trace_id, span_id Links a log to a trace. 4bf92f35... The OpenTelemetry names. order_id, customer_id Ids of the domain. order_id=12345 The same names as in the API. error_code A stable error code. ORDER_NOT_FOUND See Errors. duration_seconds The time taken. duration_seconds=0.12 A base unit, as for metrics. Some log systems use duration_ms; keep one unit.

Log levels: trace, debug, info, warn, error, fatal. These match the severity names of OpenTelemetry. Use the levels of your library and write them in lower case.

docs.title: Bad → better
docs.text:
Bad Better Why request_duration_ms http_request_duration_seconds A base unit. orders_placed orders_placed_total A counter ends with _total. avg_latency http_request_duration_seconds (a histogram) Compute the average in the query. request_duration_histogram http_request_duration_seconds Do not put the type in the name. orders_service_http_requests_total shop_http_requests_total{service="orders"} The service is a label. The prefix names the application. user_id as a label a log field or a span attribute Too many values. span GET /v1/orders/12345 GET /v1/orders/{order_id} A low-cardinality name. memory_mb memory_usage_bytes A base unit.

See also

  • Systems overview, Feature flags and Errors
  • Prometheus: metric and label naming, OpenTelemetry semantic conventions, OpenTelemetry: metric naming

docs.title: REST
docs.text:
General patterns

  • Name a resource with a plural noun: /v1/orders, /v1/customers
  • Put the id of one resource after the collection: /v1/orders/{order_id}
  • Use the HTTP method as the verb. Do not put a verb in the path for a standard action
  • Name a custom action with a verb after a colon: POST /v1/orders/{order_id}:cancel
  • Use one case style for all JSON fields and query parameters
  • Put the version first in the path: /v1/

Useful tips

  • Keep the path nesting to two levels: /v1/customers/{customer_id}/orders. For a deeper link, use a query filter
  • Use the same word in the path, in the field and in the database: customer_id
  • Name a request and a response type from the method and the resource: ListOrdersRequest, ListOrdersResponse
  • Follow the Google API Improvement Proposals (AIP) when you have no style guide of your own

General anti-patterns

  • A verb in the path for a standard action: /getOrders, /createOrder
  • A singular collection: /v1/order
  • A file extension in the path: /v1/orders.json
  • snake_case in one response and camelCase in another
  • A name from the database that leaks in the API: tbl_orders, order_fk

The examples use an e-commerce shop. Where this guide differs from the AIPs, the text says so. For names inside a database, see Databases.

docs.title: Resource paths
docs.text:
Rule Examples Why this name Collection: plural noun /v1/orders, /v1/products The path names a set. Item: collection plus id /v1/orders/{order_id} The id picks one member. Nested collection /v1/customers/{customer_id}/orders Orders that belong to one customer. Nested item /v1/customers/{customer_id}/orders/{order_id} A third level makes the path long, so use a filter instead. Singleton /v1/customers/{customer_id}/profile One profile for each customer. Multi-word segment /v1/shipping-addresses or /v1/shippingAddresses See the conflict below. Path variable {order_id} (house style) The resource name and id say what the value is. AIP-122 writes {order}. Collection name, not a verb /v1/payments Not /v1/makePayment.

Conflict: AIP-122 asks for lowerCamelCase collection ids (shippingAddresses). The Microsoft REST guidelines allow kebab-case (shipping-addresses) or camelCase. Choose one and do not mix them.

docs.title: Standard methods
docs.text:
AIP-131 to AIP-135 define five standard methods. The table shows how they map to HTTP.

Method HTTP Path Request type Response type Get GET /v1/orders/{order_id} GetOrderRequest Order List GET /v1/orders ListOrdersRequest ListOrdersResponse Create POST /v1/orders CreateOrderRequest Order Update PATCH /v1/orders/{order_id} UpdateOrderRequest Order Delete DELETE /v1/orders/{order_id} DeleteOrderRequest empty

The response of a list method holds the items in a plural field and a token for the next page: orders, next_page_token.

docs.title: Custom methods
docs.text:
AIP-136 names a custom method with a colon and a verb after the resource.

Endpoint Meaning Why this name POST /v1/orders/{order_id}:cancel Cancel one order. A verb for an action that is not a standard method. POST /v1/orders/{order_id}:ship Mark an order as shipped. A verb after a colon, as in :cancel. POST /v1/orders/{order_id}:refund Refund an order. A verb after a colon, as in :cancel. GET /v1/orders:batchGet Get many orders in one call (AIP-231). A verb on the collection. POST /v1/products:search Search with a body that is too big for a query. search is a verb on the collection. POST /v1/customers/{customer_id}:merge Merge two customers. A verb after a colon, as in :cancel. POST /v1/orders/{order_id}/cancellation The same as :cancel, written as a sub-resource (community practice). An alternative style when the action has its own state.

Conflict: some APIs avoid the colon form and use a sub-resource such as /cancellation. Choose one form for the API.

docs.title: More endpoint examples
docs.text: Endpoint Meaning GET /v1/products List products. GET /v1/products/{product_id} Get one product. GET /v1/products/{product_id}/reviews List the reviews of a product. POST /v1/products/{product_id}/reviews Create a review. GET /v1/customers List customers. GET /v1/customers/{customer_id}/addresses List the addresses of a customer. PATCH /v1/customers/{customer_id} Change some fields of a customer. DELETE /v1/customers/{customer_id}/addresses/{address_id} Delete one address. GET /v1/orders/{order_id}/items List the items of an order. POST /v1/orders/{order_id}/items Add an item. GET /v1/orders/{order_id}/payments List the payments of an order. GET /v1/carts/{cart_id} Get a cart. POST /v1/carts/{cart_id}:checkout Start the checkout of a cart. GET /v1/coupons/{coupon_id} Get a coupon. POST /v1/coupons/{coupon_id}:redeem Redeem a coupon. GET /v1/shipments/{shipment_id}/tracking-events List the tracking events. GET /v1/me Get the current user. A common alias. GET /v1/health A health check for a load balancer. GET /v1/orders/{order_id}/invoice The invoice of an order (a singleton). PATCH /v1/customers/{customer_id}/preferences Update a singleton (AIP-156 allows Get and Update).

docs.title: Query parameters
docs.text: Purpose Parameter Examples Why this name Filter by value the field name ?status=pending, ?customer_id=42 The same name as the field, so no new word to learn. Filter by range (community practice) <field>_after, <field>_before ?created_after=2026-11-01, ?created_before=2026-12-01 The field name says which date the bound is for. Filter expression filter ?filter=status = "pending" AND total_amount_cents > 10000 AIP-160 defines a filter language. Microsoft guidelines use $filter. Sort order_by ?order_by=created_at desc AIP-132 uses order_by with a direction. Sort, short form sort ?sort=-created_at JSON:API uses a leading minus. Fields to return read_mask (AIP-157); fields is community practice ?read_mask=id,status,total_amount_cents The caller asks only for the fields it needs. JSON:API writes fields[type]. Include a related resource include or expand ?include=items, ?expand[]=customer JSON:API uses include. Stripe uses expand[]. Microsoft guidelines use $expand. Search text (community practice) q or query ?q=blue+shirt A short name that many search APIs use. Show deleted items show_deleted ?show_deleted=true AIP-135 uses this name. Validate only validate_only ?validate_only=true AIP-163: a request that checks a change and does not apply it.

docs.title: Pagination
docs.text:
AIP-158 defines token pagination. Other APIs use limit and offset or a page number. Choose one style for the whole API.

Style Request Response Examples Token (AIP-158) page_size, page_token next_page_token ?page_size=50&page_token=ey... Cursor (community practice; Stripe: starting_after, has_more) limit, cursor or after next_cursor ?limit=50&after=ord_123 Offset limit, offset total_count ?limit=50&offset=100 Page number page, per_page page, total_pages ?page=3&per_page=50 Case Rule Example Last page An empty next_page_token "next_page_token": "" page_size of 0 or missing Use a default page_size omitted returns the default (for example 50) page_size above the maximum Reduce it to the maximum With a maximum of 100, page_size=10000 returns 100 items page_size below zero Return 400 page_size=-1 returns INVALID_ARGUMENT offset past the end (common practice) Return 200 with an empty list offset=9999 returns "orders": [] Bad page_token Return 400 page_token=abc returns INVALID_ARGUMENT Token from another query Should return 400 (AIP-158) A token is valid for the same filter and sort only

docs.title: Request and response types
docs.text: Kind Pattern Examples Get Get<Resource>Request GetOrderRequest List List<Resources>Request, List<Resources>Response ListOrdersRequest, ListOrdersResponse Create Create<Resource>Request CreateOrderRequest Update Update<Resource>Request UpdateOrderRequest Delete Delete<Resource>Request DeleteOrderRequest Custom <Verb><Resource>Request CancelOrderRequest, RefundOrderRequest Batch BatchGet<Resources>Request BatchGetOrdersRequest Field of a list response the plural resource name orders, products

docs.title: Fields and headers
docs.text:
Kind Rule Examples JSON field one style: snake_case or camelCase next_page_token or nextPageToken Identifier <resource>_id customer_id, order_id Timestamp <event>_at, in UTC and RFC 3339 (AIP-142 uses create_time) created_at, shipped_at Money an integer in minor units plus a currency code total_amount_cents, currency_code Boolean (AIP-140 omits the is_ prefix) is_ or has_ plus a word in this guide is_active Request id X-Request-Id (a legacy form that is still common) X-Request-Id: 7d9a... Idempotency Idempotency-Key (Stripe, and an IETF draft) Idempotency-Key: 9c1f... Concurrency ETag, If-Match If-Match: "v3" Custom header a clear name; avoid X- for new ones (RFC 6648) Request-Id, Deprecation

Conflict: the JSON style guide of Google uses camelCase. The AIP rules use snake_case in the protocol definition and camelCase in the JSON form. Many public APIs use snake_case. The choice matters less than the rule that all fields use the same one.

docs.title: Versioning
docs.text:
Style Example Notes Path /v1/orders, /v2/orders AIP-185 puts the major version in the path. Easy to see in logs. Header Stripe-Version: 2024-06-20 Stripe uses date-based versions in a header. Azure uses an api-version query parameter. Media type Accept: application/vnd.shop.v2+json Hard to try in a browser. Package shop.orders.v1 Used in Protobuf and gRPC.
